The Localization Data Science and Engineering team is at the forefront of removing language barriers and providing a stellar member experience to all our members regardless of their language preferences. We are responsible for the translation and cultural adaptation of all aspects of member interaction, including beautiful localized user interfaces, subtitles, and dubbing of award-winning Netflix originals.

We are looking for an experienced Machine Learning Scientist to join our growing team. In this role, you will build causal and machine learning models to evaluate the impact of localization algos, partner with teammates to support localization algo strategy, and train supervised ML models for localization use cases. You will also partner with a talented cross-functional team of engineers, scientists, product managers, and domain experts to shape localization strategy and deliver business impact.

Responsibilities

  • Act as strategic partner for researchers and engineers to guide localization algo development

  • Define and execute on roadmaps for measuring localization member impact and improving localization member experience with Causal Inference and Machine Learning tools

  • Partner closely with other business leaders, product managers, and other data scientists to refine and scale your findings

  • Present your research and insights to all levels of the company

  • Become a regional expert on Localization Data Science and Engineering, helping educate and connect with regional offices

About you

  • Proven track record of researching and leading Causal Inference, Machine Learning, and AI Evaluation methods in ambiguous and complex areas with a focus on technical rigor and robustness

  • High proficiency in standard tech stack (e.g., R, Python, SQL), Causal Inference (e.g., propensity score matching, double machine learning), and Machine Learning (Supervised Learning, LLM Evaluation methods)

  • 4+ years of relevant experience with Causal Inference and Machine Learning applications

  • Exceptional communication and collaboration skills coupled with strong business acumen

  • Comfortable with ambiguity; able to take ownership, and thrive with minimal oversight and process

  • Netflix culture resonates with you

That said, we are looking for the founding members of this new business area for Netflix! 

 The Creative & Policy DSE team design, develop, and operate algorithms governing creative understanding and policy enforcement, leveraging multimodal LLMs/VLMs. We focus on using Machine Learning & AI to auto-review creatives, assign attributes, and enforce policy restrictions. Your team is also responsible for extracting insights from Creative data and providing guidance to the business, both strategically and operationally. You are expected to build and lead a strong team with ML/AI and analytical talents, partner closely with Product & Engineering, and operate in a 0 - 1 space with high ambiguity. 

Responsibilities 

  • Hire, inspire, and grow high-performing Machine Learning Scientists, Analytics Engineers, and Data Scientists.

  • Lead strong partnerships with stakeholders from across the business - from product, engineering, to consumer insights, content, and strategy.

  • Instill an inclusive culture that is innovative and collaborative, both within your team and in the broader organization.

  • Develop a team charter and roadmap that optimizes the impact of the team and reflects evolving business needs.

  • Act as an ambassador between the Product, Engineering, Strategy, and DSE teams by having a deep knowledge of how the Netflix Ads product works.

  • Ensure that your team is producing consistently trustworthy and high-quality technical outputs that influence & impact the business.

About You (Requirements)

  • Demonstrated tenacity, resilience, and leadership experience that enables you to organize and drive cross-functional projects, overcome challenges, and propose solutions. 

  • Be both quantitative and qualitative. You should be able to quickly assess and understand complex systems, but also have high EQ, so that you can be a product ambassador to the rest of the organization.

  • You are a player-coach. You can develop roadmaps and strategy, but also execute on technical work and ensure that your team produces consistent high quality outputs.

  • Superb communication skills - You must be able to cultivate strong working relationships, communicate effectively, write meticulously, and give outstanding presentations to both technical and creative audiences. 

  • Experience working with multimodal LLMs, VLMs.

  • Experience building and leading hybrid Analytics, Data and ML teams in the Ads space.

  • Capacity and passion to translate business objectives into actionable analyses, and use analytics to guide product and business with quantitative recommendations.

  • A passion for TV and movies and defining the future of entertainment.

We are seeking a Senior Tax Analyst with multi-jurisdictional expertise on tax advisory for our LATAM operations (excluding Brazil), based out of our Mexico City office. This role demands a versatile tax professional who can navigate diverse regulatory frameworks across LATAM, an ever-evolving business, and the fast-paced world of production taxes and incentives.


You will combine hands-on tax advisory support with the day-to-day operations related to Production Incentives, serving as a key liaison between internal teams, external business partners, external advisors, tax authorities and film commissions across the region. 


You will report to the Sr. Tax Manager, LATAM in Mexico City and will work closely with cross-functional partners across Finance, Legal, and tax teams all around the world. The ideal candidate thrives in ambiguity and in a fast paced environment, moves comfortably between jurisdictions, and brings the flexibility to shift priorities as regulatory and business landscapes change. 


Responsibilities

Your primary responsibilities will be providing regional tax advisory and production tax/incentives support. Your day-to-day activities will include:


  • Stay current on legislative and regulatory changes across all covered jurisdictions; proactively assess their impact and advise tax leadership and stakeholders accordingly.
  • Provide tax advisory support on cross-border transactions, double taxation treaty application, business expansions, VAT refunds, production related tax questions and other regional tax matters.
  • Own the application, compliance, monetization, and reporting processes to claim Production Incentives in the region, including quarter-end close reporting.
  • Provide advisory support on the LATAM Production Incentives to local, cross-regional and cross-functional teams. 
  • Support the Sr. Manager in building and maintaining relationships with tax authorities and film commissions related to Production Tax and Incentives matters. This includes working very closely with our government relations teams and supporting public policy efforts related to Production Incentives.
  • Coordinate and drive tax audits across the region— tax authority and/or any government inquiries—owning the end-to-end audit lifecycle from initial response through resolution, navigating cross-functional alignment and collaboration.
  • Support the Sr. Manager on ad-hoc projects such as creation of new legal entities, new business initiatives, tax program applications, VAT refunds and electronic invoicing/requirements changes.
  • Support the LATAM Tax team on tax compliance, month end close, and day-to-day activities as needed.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting and/or Law.
  • 8+ years of relevant experience in tax compliance, with proven multi-country expertise across LATAM (Mexico required; Colombia, Argentina, Perú and extraterritorial/digital service taxes strongly preferred).
  • In-depth knowledge of direct and indirect tax regulations in Mexico and LATAM countries; familiarity with country-specific platforms (e.g., SAT, DIAN, AFIP, SUNAT) is desirable.
  • Demonstrated experience managing tax audits—statutory, tax authority, and government inquiries—from planning through resolution in at least two LATAM jurisdictions.
  • Experience with Production Tax and Incentives is highly desirable.
  • Highly proficient in spreadsheets and memo writing; knowledge of Workday, Blackline, Google suite and electronic invoicing systems is a plus.
  • Highly organized with the ability to balance competing priorities and navigate multiple deadlines across jurisdictions simultaneously. Can lean into GenAI to improve the quality and speed of work.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills; able to convey complex tax nuances to a diverse audience clearly and succinctly. Able to deeply analyze, clearly communicate (verbally and in writing) knowledge and advise in plain and clear terms.
  • Hands-on mentality with a problem-solving approach; passionate about helping drive the business forward.
  • High degree of flexibility and adaptability; comfortable operating across different tax regimes and cultural contexts.
  • Fluent in Spanish and English (written and spoken).

Overview

Microsoft Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Teams, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with our server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for engineers to help achieve that mission.

The Compute Silicon & Manufacturing Engineering (CSME) organization within SCHIE is responsible for design, development, manufacturing and packaging of Microsoft's state-of-the-art computer chips, notably the Azure Cobalt. Our solutions provide sustainable strategic advantages to Microsoft and enable our customers to achieve more.

As Microsoft's cloud business continues to grow the ability to deploy new offerings and hardware infrastructure on time, in high volume with high quality and lowest cost is of paramount importance. To achieve this goal, the Shared and Custom IP & Silicon (SCIPS) team is instrumental in defining and elivering operational measures of success for hardware manufacturing, improving the planning process, quality, delivery, scale and sustainability related to Microsoft cloud hardware. We are looking for engineers with a dedicated passion for customer focused solutions, insight and industry knowledge to envision and implement future technical solutions that will manage and optimize the Cloud infrastructure.

We are looking for a Principal Silicon Security Architect to lead security architecture for Microsoft custom silicon and SoC platforms. You will translate product threats, customer requirements, and platform security goals into actionable hardware, firmware, and software security architectures. The role spans threat modeling, hardware roots of trust, secure boot and lifecycle management, attestation, confidential computing, isolation, secure debug, cryptographic services, provisioning, physical attack resistance, and security validation. You will partner across system, silicon, IP, firmware, software, verification, validation, and external engineering teams from early concept through production and post-silicon security closure.  

#SCHIE #CSME  #SCIPS

The candidate for this position will be expected and able to complete the following responsibilities:

The Cloud & AI organization accelerates Microsoft's mission to ensure that our company and industry is securing digital technology platforms, devices, and clouds in our customers' heterogeneous environments, as well as ensuring the security of our own internal estate. Our culture is centered on embracing a growth mindset, a theme of inspiring excellence, and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their best each day. In doing so, we create life-changing innovations that impact billions of lives around the world.

Are you passionate about emulating the world's most determined adversaries – and about teaching machines to do it alongside you? Join the Microsoft Red Team (MRT) organization, where we emulate real-world advanced persistent threats to ensure Microsoft, and the customers who depend on us, are prepared to face and respond to any adversary.

CyberShield is the MRT program that extends our red team capability beyond Microsoft's own estate to select external customers. Our mandate is to shift red teaming from point-in-time, human-led engagements to a software-driven, continuous model powered by agentic, AI-driven red teaming. CyberShield operators work across Microsoft's own environment and customer environments spanning cloud, identity, network, endpoint, hardware, and operational security domains, and partner closely with Microsoft's adversary hunting organization to present a unified front to the customers we defend together.

We are looking for a Principal Security Engineer to serve as a principal-level operator on CyberShield engagements. You will plan and execute full-scope adversary emulation operations end-to-end, and – critically – you will drive agentic, AI-driven red team operations: designing, directing, and supervising autonomous and semi-autonomous agents that discover, chain, and exploit weaknesses at a scale and cadence no human-only team can match. You will be a forward-deployed technical authority in front of customer security leaders, a trusted peer to senior engineers across MRT, and a force multiplier who raises the technical bar for every operator and agent on the team.

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day.

Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for passionate engineers to help achieve that mission. 

As Microsoft's cloud business continues to grow the ability to deploy new offerings and hardware infrastructure on time, in high volume with high quality and lowest cost is of paramount importance. To achieve this goal, the AI Silicon Architecture team is instrumental in defining and delivering operational measures of success for hardware manufacturing, improving the planning process, quality, delivery, scale and sustainability related to Microsoft cloud hardware. We are looking for engineers with a dedicated passion for customer focused solutions, insight and industry knowledge to envision and implement future technical solutions that will manage and optimize the Cloud infrastructure.  

We are looking for a Principal AI Silicon Architect to join the team.

  • Own end-to-end power architecture for high-power AI accelerator SoCs, including tradeoff analysis not only for SOC, but expand to package, board, and system. 
  • Define SoC and package-level power-management architecture, including power/voltage domains, DVFS, clock and power gating, low-power states, workload-aware power management, and other power-saving mechanisms. 
  • Define architectures for high-power operating conditions, including management of workload power excursions, peak power, sustained power, transient behavior, and power/thermal constraints.

Azure Front Door powers application delivery, acceleration, security, load management, and Internet routing for Microsoft, LinkedIn, Azure, Microsoft 365, Xbox, and thousands of customers worldwide. The service operates one of the largest edge networks in the industry, processing massive amounts of traffic across a globally distributed fleet. The existing AFD Senior Engineer template emphasizes building globally distributed, scalable, low-latency services that power critical Microsoft and Azure workloads.


We are looking for a hands-on Senior Software Engineer to join Azure Front Door's Linux Infrastructure team. This team owns the foundational Linux platform that powers AFD's global edge fleet, including operating system lifecycle, Kubernetes infrastructure, fleet management, security, performance optimization, and platform reliability. We are not looking for architects who primarily build roadmaps. We are looking for engineers who can independently drive complex initiatives from idea to production, solve difficult system-level problems, and lead small crews of engineers to deliver meaningful customer impact.

You will help shape the future of Azure Front Door by enabling adoption of the latest innovations across Linux, Kubernetes, hardware acceleration, networking, operating systems, and security technologies. Overview

The People Operations Center of Excellence enables People Operations services at scale. It simplifies and standardises processes, improves data quality and delivers a seamless employee experience across Microsoft. People Operations provides centralised HR support: it handles employee inquiries, manages HR transactions, and uses digital and AI solutions to improve service delivery.

Within this model, the EMEA Offboarding team manages end-to-end employee exits across around 50 countries and many different legal and regulatory environments. The team makes sure every exit is compliant, accurate and on time. This includes sensitive and complex terminations, severance and payroll inputs, termination documents, and coordination with stakeholders. The team's scope is growing. Offboarding is taking ownership of more termination activity once the decision to terminate has been made, including work moving over from People Consulting & Engagement (PC&E).

As a Senior HR Service Advisor (Offboarding – EMEA), you will handle complex offboarding cases from start to finish, including involuntary terminations, job eliminations and other sensitive exits. You will work closely with the business, PC&E, Payroll and vendors. You will also coach advisors in the team and contribute to a more standardised, automated and resilient offboarding model.



Responsibilities

Case management and complex exits

  • Manage offboarding cases from start to finish, including complex and sensitive ones, for employees and managers across EMEA.
  • Process voluntary & involuntary terminations once the decision to terminate has been made.
  • Prepare termination documents, notifications, severance components and payroll inputs, making sure they are accurate and compliant with local law.
  • Support preparation before a termination, such as simulations, calculations and readiness checks with PC&E and the business.
  • Support large restructures (RIFs) in waves: prepare documents and calculations, and coordinate payroll inputs for groups of employees.
  • Handle bereavement and other highly sensitive cases with empathy, discretion and confidentiality.

Stakeholder and vendor coordination

  • Work with business leaders, local HR partners, payroll and Legal on termination actions. Give clear guidance on process, timelines and what is needed operationally.
  • Coordinate Payroll, Benefits, Immigration, Mobility, company car providers and other vendors so exits run smoothly.
  • Act as the first escalation point within the team for issues affecting delivery, compliance or the employee experience. Escalate further with clear recommendations.

Data, compliance and audit

  • Keep data in HR systems accurate and in line with local labour law, global policies and data privacy requirements.
  • Coordinate final settlements and severance payments with Payroll. Spot and fix discrepancies early.
  • Support statutory and internal audit requests, for example by gathering signed termination documents and evidence for authorities.
  • Identify and reduce compliance risks in country-specific and high-risk termination cases.

Team capability and knowledge

  • Partner in creating guidance for termination processing and teamwork within POPS 
  • Help onboard and train new joiners. Act as the go-to expert for selected countries or termination types.
  • Create and update step-by-step process guidelines (DTPs), knowledge articles, templates and workflows, especially for complex termination types.

Process improvement and automation

  • Find opportunities to simplify, standardise and automate offboarding processes.
  • Help introduce new tools, workflows and integrations, including Power Apps solutions, ADP integration and the Employee Self-Service Agent.
  • Use AI and digital tools to reduce manual work and improve quality.
  • Track performance metrics and contribute to improvements in quality, speed and fewer escalations.


Qualifications

Required Qualification:

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Operations or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • At least 3 years of experience in HR operations, HR shared services or employee lifecycle management.
  • Fluent English, spoken and written.

 

Preferred Qualification:

  • Experience handling complex or sensitive HR cases, such as involuntary terminations, escalations or compliance-driven processes.
  • Experience with HR systems and case management tools. SAP SuccessFactors (Employee Central), Dynamics CRM or similar are an advantage.
  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, including working with business leaders and other HR teams.
  • Knowledge of EMEA labour law, payroll processes and data privacy (GDPR) requirements.
  • Interest in automation, AI tools or process improvement (for example Power Apps or Copilot).

Overview

Microsoft Industry Solutions – Global Center for Innovation and Delivery (GCID) delivers end‑to‑end, industry‑aligned solutions by accelerating customer adoption of Microsoft technologies. With a global team of 1,000+ professionals, GCID offers early‑career engineers a collaborative environment to work on real‑world customer challenges and build consulting, cloud, and application development skills. 

 

As a Consultant – Full Stack AI Application Developer (Azure), you will contribute to the design, development, and deployment of modern cloud‑based applications, partnering with senior engineers and architects. This role is ideal for developers eager to strengthen full‑stack skills, deepen Azure expertise, and gain exposure to AI‑enabled application patterns in enterprise delivery. 

 



Responsibilities
  • Design and build cloud‑native, full‑stack applications on Microsoft Azure, contributing across UI, API, services, and data layers with high‑quality, secure, and scalable code. 
  • Collaborate with architects and senior consultants to translate business requirements into technical designs and implementation plans; participate in design reviews and solution walkthroughs. 
  • Own feature delivery end‑to‑end: estimate effort, implement features, write unit/integration tests, perform code reviews, and support deployment through CI/CD pipelines. 
  • Integrate backend services and data platforms, implement RESTful APIs, and ensure performance, reliability, and observability (logging, metrics, traces) for production readiness. 
  • Apply security, compliance, and Responsible AI principles across application development and operations, following Microsoft and customer governance standards. 
  • Identify technical risks and dependencies early; raise and help mitigate issues, support technical escalations, and contribute to contingency plans for smooth delivery. 
  • Reuse and contribute to shared frameworks and IP, leveraging best practices, accelerators, and patterns to improve delivery speed and predictability. 
  • Collaborate cross‑functionally (e.g., project leads, delivery managers, account teams) to articulate technical value, support adoption, and ensure customer outcomes.
  • Continuously learn and improve, adopt modern engineering practices (DevSecOps, automation, testing, cloud monitoring) and sharing learnings with the team. 


Qualifications

  • 4-10 years of professional software development experience. 

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, Engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience. 

  • Microsoft or cloud certifications are preferred, including but not limited to: 
    MCSD/MCAD/MCSE, AZ‑204, AI‑900, AI‑102, or equivalent entry‑ to mid‑level cloud and AI certifications.

Full‑Stack Application Development 

  • Hands‑on experience designing and building applications using .NET (C#), .NET Web APIs, Node.js with modern front‑end technologies such as JavaScript or TypeScript, and frameworks like Angular or React. 

  • Strong understanding of application development across UI, API, service, integration, and data layers. 

  • Experience building and consuming RESTful services and integrating backend systems. 

  • Working knowledge of relational databases such as Azure SQL, Azure Cosmos DB, PostgreSQL, Azure SQL managed Instance or Azure Database for MySQL, including data access and performance considerations. 

  • Solid foundation in software engineering principles, including clean code, debugging, testing, and problem‑solving. 

AI‑Enabled Application Development  

  • Hands‑on experience integrating AI capabilities into applications, such as search, chat, recommendations, or content generation using AI services or APIs. 

  • Practical knowledge of Azure AI services, including Azure AI Foundry and Azure AI Search, and understanding of RAG (Retrieval‑Augmented Generation) patterns. 

  • Experience with RAG pipelines, vector search workflows, or agent‑based patterns using tools such as Semantic Kernel, LangChain, or similar frameworks. 

  • Experience with prompt engineering and optimization to build reliable, high‑quality AI‑driven application workflows. 

  • Working knowledge of Python for implementing AI workflows, automation, or AI‑assisted application components. 

  • Understanding and application of Responsible AI principles in designing and delivering AI‑enabled solutions. 

Cloud & DevOps 

  • Experience working with Microsoft Azure for application hosting, configuration, and deployment. 

  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines, source control (Git), and automated build and release processes. 

  • Basic experience with application monitoring, logging, and troubleshooting in cloud environments. 

  • Understanding secure application development practices, including authentication and authorization. 

Good‑to‑Have / Preferred Skills 

  • Exposure to evaluation and tuning techniques for improving AI response quality and reliability.  

  • Familiarity with microservices and serverless architectures, including Azure Functions, containers, or Kubernetes. 

  • Awareness of deployment strategies such as blue/green or canary releases. 

  • Exposure to end‑to‑end observability concepts (metrics, traces).  

  • Experience with open‑source technologies or familiarity with platforms beyond Azure (e.g., Java, AWS, or Google Cloud Platform). 

  • Domain exposure to industries such as financial services, healthcare, manufacturing, or retail. 

 

Consulting Mindset & Collaboration 

  • Ability to work closely with senior consultants, architects, and customers to co-create innovative solutions with customers to help solve their business challenges 

  • Strong communication skills to explain technical concepts to business stakeholders 

  • Comfortable working in ambiguous environments, learning quickly, and adapting to change 

  • Eagerness to build engineering excellence, reusable components, and best practices 

Growth & Learning Orientation 

  • Strong interest in continuous learning and technical certifications 

  • Curiosity to explore emerging data and AI technologies 

  • Willingness to receive feedback, grow technical depth, and expand ownership over time

Other  

  • Embody our culture and values

Overview

We are the Windows Servicing and Delivery (WSD) organization, dedicated to keeping over 1.8 billion Windows devices secure and productive by delivering timely updates and innovations to all versions of Windows.  Our work helps to protect users and their mission critical infrastructure in a fast-changing security landscape. We create and support new business opportunities across Microsoft, especially with the large and growing Windows installation base. We build delightful experiences for our customers and build products and solutions to empower our commercial and enterprise customers to keep their devices secure, compliant and up to date with latest innovations in Windows.

We are looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to lead a team of TPMs and Product Managers across Windows Server and Networking, two foundational areas that power enterprise workloads and experiences across the Windows ecosystem. You will work closely with engineering, product, security, servicing, and customer-facing teams to identify the highest-impact customer problems, translate them into clear priorities, and drive programs from strategy through execution and customer impact.

This role requires a leader who is equally comfortable going deep into complex technical problems and stepping back to understand the broader product, customer, and business context. You will help your team navigate ambiguity, make the right technical and product tradeoffs, use data and customer signals to drive decisions, and influence teams across organizational boundaries. You will lead and grow a high-performing team of PMs, creating clarity and accountability while developing their technical depth, product judgment, and leadership capabilities. You will attract, develop, and retain outstanding talent and build an inclusive environment where people can do their best work.

As an AI-First leader, you will incorporate and coach your team on the responsible and effective use of AI across product management and engineering execution. You will also help identify opportunities where AI can fundamentally improve how we understand customer problems, diagnose and manage Windows systems, and deliver secure and reliable experiences at scale.

We value passion, creativity, drive, agility, accountability, technical curiosity, and a desire to continuously learn. Our customers are at the heart of everything we do, and delivering exceptional Windows experiences is our top priority. If you're excited about leading and developing a solid PM organization, shaping critical Windows Server and Networking investments, solving difficult technical and customer problems, and creating impact at Windows scale, we would love to hear from you.

Microsoft's CO+I team is seeking a Datacenter Engineering Procurement Construction (EPC) Integrated Planner / Scheduler Lead to provide services for Johor Bahru Metro/Site in MALAYSIA. The employee will provide integrated planning and schedule management services for the campus. They will be required to develop and analyze totally integrated engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) schedules. Recommend solutions or recovery plans to schedule or cost impact or delays. Required weekly and monthly reporting as assigned. 

We utilize tools such as Master Schedules, Risk Framework, Quality Checklists and Schedule Health Scorecards, and are hands-on with the PMs in the field, and with the General Contractor with our tools and analysis.  This results in Schedule Predictability driving overall delivery efficiencies.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. This role is a field-based role for the JOHOR BAHRU metro. Relocation support will be provided, and successful candidates must ​relocate or reside within 50 miles of the field location. This role is not eligible for hybrid or remote work.



Responsibilities

Responsibilities:

Planning

  • Develop Integrated EPC Master Schedules (IMS) including timelines and dependencies for large-scale datacenter construction projects.
  • Work with cross-functional teams, including engineers, procurement, and construction to ensure project milestones are met and deliverables are completed on time.
  • Monitor project risks and develop contingency plans to mitigate potential issues.
  • Study the delay events and their impact to the EPC schedule and present to stakeholders, Regional planning lead.
  • Work with clients to understand their needs and ensure project outcomes meet their expectations.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with key stakeholders
  • Continuously improve project management processes and tools to increase efficiency and effectiveness.

General Contractor (GC) Procurement & Construction Schedule Baseline Management

  • Facilitate and support the development of a detailed EPC Project Schedule along with Regional leads, project team, GC and Sub-Contractor vendors.
  • Work closely with the Regional Planning Lead to ensure the GC Baseline Schedule meets the standards and requirements defined within the DIV1 Specification.
  • Complete the GC Baseline Evaluation process and provide recommendations in MSFT formats.
  • Carry out the GC Proposal Schedule Evaluations and provide evaluation narrative and scores.

Schedule Analysis and Reporting

  • Facilitate and participate in weekly schedule reviews onsite with GC schedule teams to analyze and validate progress onsite.
  • Proactively analyze project schedules by; comparing cost and resource curves to actuals, tracking float consumption, perform schedule integrity (health) and quality checks, critical path analysis, analyze quantity progress curves, schedule performance index, carry-out delay impact analysis, monitor monthly performance and carry out variance analysis supporting Baseline Management and Change Control processes throughout the Project Lifecycle
  • Carry out and communicate Schedule Time Impact Assessments (EOT) of schedule delay events and recommend mitigation strategies to recover and/or control the impacts.
  • Record reasons for delay and quantification with all supporting documentation on a regular basis to enable protect owners interest supporting and providing inputs to claims management process.
  • Ensure GC compliance with MSFT Monthly and Weekly reporting cadence and Rhythm of Business requirements.
  • Evaluate GC Weekly and Monthly Schedule Reports, validate progress, review insights with EPC PMs and provides feedback and recommendations to GC.  
  • Validate schedule updates along with a narrative for submission to the project team and MSFT stakeholders.
  • Identify and mitigate threats to the project's schedule and initiate corrective actions through field staff.
  • Analyze resource loading and recommend adjustments / corrective action as appropriate.
  • Assess impacts of design and/or long lead equipment changes and provide recommendations to mitigate/recover the schedule.
  • Provide final review of schedules for estimating as requested.

Collaboration

  • Lead collaborative Planning workshops by using the Schedule to help facilitate planning, coordination, and accurate progress reporting. 
  • Interface with site management regarding critical schedule activities, change, impacts to schedule, change orders, project progress, and claims analysis.
  • Provide planning and schedule management support to DCD PMs, MSFT stakeholders, project teams and Redmond-based hub.
  • Support the Regional and Global Scheduling Leads with the formulation, implementation and ongoing development of scheduling processes and procedures, data and report collation, data analysis.  
  • Demonstrates leadership, accountability.

Rhythm of Business

  • Adhere to MSFT Rhythm of Business deliverables for your project.
  • Review and evaluate GC Schedule submittals.
  • Complete on-time Month End Project reports and review with EPC PMs.
  • Review Month End Project Report and evaluation findings with the GC and follow up on action items.
  • Support the Regional Schedule Lead in preparing for Monthly Regional Review.
  • Record lessons learnt and implement to improve the DIV1 specs and other procedures

  • Bachelor’s degree in construction project management, Architecture, Engineering, or related field and 10+ years related experience

  • 10+ years of experience in planning and scheduling medium sized capital projects ($50MM USD - $200MM+ USD) in data center, oil and gas or chemicals (or related process industry). This experience should specifically include engineering and procurement, with specific examples of integrated construction planning. 
  • Excellent understanding of Project Planning, Earned Value Management and Key Commodity Tracking.
  • Excellent skills in Oracle P6 project planning software
  • Strong familiarity with CPM scheduling methodology.
  • Familiarity with Schedule Risk Analysis.
  • Ability to analyze EPC plans/schedule and provide deep insights into trends, issues, mitigations.
  • Good verbal, written communication skills
  • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and prioritize tasks effectively.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to deliver high-quality work.
  • Experience in managing teams and working collaboratively with cross-functional groups.

  • Ability to present data from a detailed to high-level depending on audience.

Imagine the web itself as your raw material — every page, every image, every signal of what’s new and what matters, flowing in at a scale most engineers only read about in systems papers.
At Apple, that scale is a daily reality. The data acquisition platform you’d help lead doesn’t just power search — it’s the sensory layer underneath Siri, Spotlight, Apple Maps, and the foundation models driving Apple Intelligence. Every one of those products depends on a continuous, exabyte-scale pipeline of fresh, high-quality information pulled from the live web, stored, and made usable in near real time.
As a Sr. Staff / Distinguished Engineer on this team, you won’t just build the pipes — you’ll shape the intelligence that decides what flows through them. This role sits at the intersection of distributed systems and machine learning: the hard problem isn’t only moving exabytes of data, it’s deciding what’s worth acquiring, how to score and prioritize it, and how to continuously improve that judgment as the web and Apple’s models evolve. You’ll work across engineering, AI research, and product teams to turn crawl and storage infrastructure into a system that gets smarter over time — one whose decisions directly shape the quality of the intelligence millions of people rely on through Apple’s products.
If you’re energized by distributed systems at their most extreme scale, know how to bring ML into the decisions that govern what data gets captured and how it’s valued, and want your judgment to shape the strategic direction of Apple’s AI data foundation, we want to talk to you.

Description

This role owns technical strategy and execution for Apple’s web-scale data acquisition platform — the systems that crawl, store, and deliver exabytes of web content and images to power Siri, Spotlight, Apple Maps, and Apple’s foundation models. Responsibilities span the full lifecycle of acquired data: crawl strategy and prioritization, the ML-driven decisions about what’s worth capturing and how to value it, and the scalable storage and compute architecture that makes all of it usable downstream.
As a senior member of the technical staff, you will set direction on how Apple acquires data efficiently, broadly, and precisely at a scale that few infrastructure problems in the industry match. The hardest problems here live at the boundary between distributed systems and machine learning: designing storage and compute that let engineering teams move fast without being bottlenecked by data gravity, while applying ML to decide what to crawl, how to score quality and relevance, and how those decisions should evolve as the web and Apple’s models change. You’ll also shape how downstream teams consume what’s acquired, to maximize its value for search ranking and AI model training alike.
Success in this role depends on working across organizational boundaries — partnering with crawl infrastructure, search indexing, and AI/foundation model teams to align architecture and ML strategy with Apple’s broader AI direction. You’ll be expected to navigate ambiguous, large-scale technical tradeoffs independently, and to act as a trusted technical voice to senior leadership on direction, risk, and resourcing for one of Apple’s most foundational data platforms.

Minimum Qualifications

12+ years building and operating distributed systems at large scale (petabyte/exabyte-class storage, compute, or data pipelines)
Demonstrated experience applying machine learning to data quality, ranking, relevance, or prioritization problems in production
Track record of setting technical direction across multiple teams as a senior lead — not just within a single team’s codebase
Experience partnering with ML/AI research teams to translate model needs into infrastructure and data requirements
B.S. in Computer Science, M.S./PhD Preferred

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with web crawling, search indexing, or large-scale content pipelines specifically
Familiarity with how training data pipelines feed large language or foundation models
History of mentoring senior engineers and influencing org-level architecture decisions

Reference Image is one of Apple's most ambitious end-to-end security and imaging initiatives: a system that lets users cryptographically verify that a photo genuinely came from an Apple device sensor, unaltered. It spans everything from the image sensor, through on-device capture and RAW pipelines, to Private Cloud Compute (PCC) processing and signing, all the way to viewing and sharing experiences across iOS and macOS.

We're looking for a Systems Engineer to join the Reference Image team and own key pieces of the technical architecture and cross-stack integration, someone who can reason across hardware security, cloud infrastructure, and application-layer behavior. You'll work under the guidance of the project DRI, taking ownership of specific systems-level work streams while helping drive alignment across a distributed, multi-team effort toward a coherent, secure, and shippable system.

Description

In this role you’ll be expected to:
* Contribute to and help maintain the systems architecture for Reference Image, spanning sensor-level signing, on-device RAW capture pipelines, and cloud-based development in PCC.
* Contribute to the design and implementation of cryptographic key rotation, certificate lifecycle management, and revocation frameworks.
* Work closely with Security and Privacy teams to help threat-model end-to-end media authenticity workflows, evaluating cryptographic integrity, data privacy, and downstream non-destructive edit handling.
* Help evaluate and advance standard and extended image container formats to support secure provenance and authenticity metadata.
* Coordinate with PCC/Cloud infrastructure teams on specific integration points to ensure the signing and certificate infrastructure scales and meets the security bar.
* Represent your work stream's technical tradeoffs in cross-functional forums (Photos, Camera Capture, ISP/hardware, QA, Privacy, Legal, Marketing), proactively identifying and resolving cross-team technical dependencies and blockers.
* Contribute to scoping and planning for future hardware generations under the direction of the DRI.

Minimum Qualifications

BS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field and 5+ years of experience in industry.
Familiarity with cryptographic signing/verification concepts (certificates, secure boot, key management, revocation) and comfort partnering closely with Security/Privacy teams.
Experience with image/media pipelines (RAW processing, ISP behavior, DNG/JPEG/HEIF formats) is a strong plus.
Experience with distributed cloud infrastructure and confidential compute environments (PCC or similar) preferred.
Ability to work effectively across many stakeholder teams (hardware, platform software, cloud, privacy, legal, QA) on ambiguous, evolving requirements, while keeping the project DRI informed of key tradeoffs and risks.
Strong communicator who can translate deep technical tradeoffs into clear guidance for both engineering and non-engineering stakeholders (e.g., legal, marketing, support).

Preferred Qualifications

Comfortable operating in a fast-moving, still-evolving system with real security stakes and public-facing implications (e.g., newsroom/wire-service use cases).
Capable of coding to fill functional gaps in the team.
Familiarity with trusted time stamping mechanisms and their role in establishing chain-of-custody for signed data.
Experience working on flagship security or trust features that ship across multiple operating systems.

Velocity at Scale: Find and remove bottlenecks across the ML lifecycle, including data loading, experiment tracking, and artifact management, so modelers spend their time on models and not on plumbing.
Quality & Privacy by Design: Build data quality checks, lineage, and governance tooling that keep our datasets and models trustworthy and consistent with Apple's privacy principles.

The Critical Facilities Lead – Electrical Infrastructure is responsible for the operational integrity, reliability, maintenance, and safety of all high-availability electrical distribution and backup power systems across the campus/critical facility.

This role serves as the subject matter expert (SME) and operational leader for mission-critical power systems—including Medium Voltage (MV) switchgear and substations, Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) systems, emergency diesel/natural gas generators, paralleling switchgear, and associated power monitoring infrastructure (EPMS/SCADA).

Responsibilities

1. Electrical Infrastructure & Asset Reliability:
Medium Voltage Distribution: Oversee the operation, inspection, and maintenance of MV switchgear (4.16 kV to 35 kV class), unit substations, dry-type/oil-filled transformers, protective relays (e.g., SEL), and vacuum/SF6 circuit breakers.
Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS: Lead maintenance, load-balancing, and lifecycle management for multi-module double-conversion static or rotary UPS systems, static transfer switches (STS), power distribution units (PDUs), and energy storage solutions (VRLA, Lithium-ion, battery strings).
Emergency Generation & Fuel Systems: Direct operational readiness, monthly no-load testing, scheduled dynamic/load-bank testing, and preventative maintenance on multi-megawatt standby generator systems, emergency fuel storage/filtration polishing systems, and automated paralleling switchgear.
Power Quality & Monitoring: Continuously monitor power quality, harmonics, power factor, and transient disturbances utilizing the Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) and SCADA platforms.

2. Operational Procedures & Risk Mitigation (MOP / SOP / EOP)
Procedure Authoring & Review: Author, review, and strictly enforce detailed Methods of Procedure (MOPs), Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and Emergency Operating Procedures (EOPs) for all planned maintenance, testing, switching operations, and contingency drills.
Switching Operations: Oversee MV and LV complex switching sequences, bypass operations, and utility-to-generator transfer scenarios to prevent unintended power interruptions.
Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Lead post-event investigations and technical root cause analyses for any power anomalies, outages, or near-misses, driving corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) to completion.

3. Electrical Safety & Regulatory Compliance
Safety Leadership: Champion the site Electrical Safety Program in full compliance with NFPA 70E, OSHA 1910 Subpart S, and NFPA 70 (NEC).
Hazard Control: Enforce strict Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) protocols, arc-flash boundary enforcement, appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) compliance, and Energized Electrical Work Permit (EEWP) processes.
Code & Environmental Compliance: Maintain compliance with local, state, and federal codes, including NFPA 110 (Emergency and Standby Power Systems), EPA air quality permits, spill prevention (SPCC) for fuel oil storage, and local environmental reporting.

4. Preventative Maintenance & CMMS Administration
Manage annual, semi-annual, quarterly, and monthly preventive/predictive maintenance programs (PM/PdM) via the site Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).
Oversee advanced non-destructive diagnostic programs: infrared (IR) thermography, breaker primary/secondary current injection testing, relay calibration, and battery internal resistance/impedance testing.
Track Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) including Planned Maintenance and Reactive Work orders completion rates, and power utilization metrics.

5. Vendor, Project & Commissioning Management
Manage specialized critical electrical service contractors (e.g., switchgear testing houses, UPS factory technicians, generator service providers, relay engineers).
Act as the operation’s technical representative for capital improvement, expansion, and equipment refresh projects.
Participate in Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), and Integrated System Testing (IST) for new electrical installations.

6. Emergency Response & Incident Command
Participate in the 24/7 technical on-call rotation for critical infrastructure system alarms, critical failures, utility interruptions, and severe weather response.
Act as incident commander or technical lead during emergency power transitions, ensuring rapid, safe fault isolation and service restoration.

Meta is seeking Security Engineers with Privacy and Data protection expertise to join our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AAI) organization. You will apply deep privacy engineering expertise to hard, real-world problems in how systems collect, use, retain, expose, and delete data. Your work is AI-augmented from day one: you leverage AI tools and agents to accelerate your impact, and where the models fall short, your expertise directly drives their improvement. The problems that matter here are the ones a capable engineer cannot solve by reading the code in front of them: which jurisdiction's deadline applies to a deletion request, whether a derived dataset clears an anonymity threshold, where a deletion has to cascade. Models already handle the privacy obligations that are stated as ordinary good engineering practice, so the work is the obligation they cannot derive. This role is for privacy engineers who want to operate at the intersection of deep privacy expertise and frontier AI, not just applying AI to privacy work but shaping what it is capable of.

Responsibilities

  • Identify and solve ambiguous problems within the privacy and data protection space where the solution and requirements are initially unknown, driving solutions that affect multiple teams
  • Architect privacy capabilities and evaluation infrastructure that sets the standard across teams; drive platform-level decisions for AI-driven privacy solutions at Meta's scale
  • Lead the strategy and methodology for the privacy problems AI cannot yet reason about: jurisdictional and regulatory obligations, de-identification standards, data lifecycle controls, and data access reasoning
  • Shape how privacy expertise translates into AI capabilities: define the methodologies that make model improvement systematic and scalable
  • Drive cross-organizational partnerships that define how privacy and AI intersect: influence technical direction beyond the immediate team
  • Break down problems into smaller scoped work streams, owning the most technically complex pieces while enabling others to execute against the overall solution
  • Mentor other engineers across the organization, build a community, and act as a role model for privacy engineering practices and Meta values
  • Disseminate findings through internal publications, knowledge sharing, and contributions to the broader privacy and security community

Minimum Qualifications

  • B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field, or equivalent experience
  • 8+ years of hands-on engineering experience in technical privacy, data protection, or privacy-adjacent security engineering
  • Deep expertise in at least one privacy subdomain with demonstrated ability to advance the state of the art: purpose limitation, retention and deletion, data access control, jurisdictional obligations, de-identification, consent, or ML and model privacy
  • Experience implementing privacy obligations in production systems, in addition to reviewing or advising on them
  • Software engineering proficiency, including code review and maintenance, with experience coding in Python, PHP, Java, C/C++, or an equivalent language
  • Track record of architecting privacy systems, controls or programs that operate at scale and influence how others build
  • Demonstrated ability to define and drive complex, ambiguous problem spaces with group-level impact

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • Experience improving AI model performance through expert feedback, red teaming, or evaluation design
  • Experience with pseudonymization lifecycle, including deletion of the user-to-pseudonym mapping
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. Reality Labs Research Audio builds the audio-visual perception that future smart glasses will rely on. That includes understanding who the wearer is talking to, who is speaking, and how a conversation is organized. To train and evaluate these models at scale, we need realistic conversation data that comes with exact ground truth. This internship explores generative models that produce such data. The project: Generate realistic video with audio of multi-person conversations. Inputs can be text alone, text plus one image of a group, or text plus a reference image for each person. Beyond looking real, the scenes should show natural social interaction: turn-taking, gaze, head orientation, listener reactions and group formations. Each scene should also be controllable: the 3D position of each person, how people are grouped, and the position and pose of the egocentric camera. That control is what lets the output serve as accurately labelled training data for audio-visual models, e.g. predicting the glasses wearer's intent or detecting conversation groups.

Responsibilities

  • Design and train video diffusion or flow-matching models for multi-person conversation scenes, generating audio and video together.
  • Develop ways to condition generation on 3D layout, group structure and egocentric camera trajectory.
  • Keep each person's identity consistent across frames and viewpoints, from one or several reference images.
  • Model natural conversational behavior: speech-driven faces and gestures, gaze, turn-taking and listener reactions.
  • Build evaluations for realism, audio-visual sync, identity consistency, and how closely the generated 3D positions and poses match the specified ones.
  • Use the generated data to train downstream egocentric perception models, and measure how much it helps.
  • Publish results at top venues together with Meta researchers.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Research experience in generative modeling for video or images, with first-author publications at venues such as CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR or SIGGRAPH
  • Hands-on experience training or fine-tuning modern video diffusion or flow-matching models (e.g. DiT-based architectures), including conditioning methods such as adapters, ControlNet or LoRA
  • Experience with controllable generation from geometric or structural signals: camera pose, 3D layout, depth or human pose
  • Solid grounding in 3D vision: camera models, multi-view geometry and coordinate transforms
  • 3+ years experience with Python, Matlab, Pytorch, large-scale distributed GPU training or similar
  • Must obtain work authorization in the country of employment at the time of hire, and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with joint audio-video generation, speech-driven talking heads or gestures, multi-speaker TTS, or lip sync
  • Background in spatial audio: binaural rendering, HRTFs, or room acoustics simulation
  • Research on modeling social interaction: conversational dynamics, gaze, turn-taking or group formations
  • Familiarity with egocentric perception and datasets (e.g. Ego4D, Ego-Exo4D, Aria), and with tasks such as active speaker detection or conversation grouping
  • Experience with 3D or 4D human and scene representations (e.g. SMPL-X, Gaussian splatting, NeRF) or multi-view-consistent video generation
  • Experience with synthetic data generation, game engines, or improving how well models trained on synthetic data perform on real data
  • Experience using LLMs or VLMs to plan scenes, layouts or dialogue
  • Track record of open-source contributions or a previous industry research internship
  • Proven track record of achieving results as demonstrated in accepted papers at top computer vision and machine learning related conferences such as CVPR, ECCV, NIPS, ICASSP, InterSpeech etc
  • Experience working and communicating cross functionally in a team environment
  • Intent to return to a degree-program after the completion of the internship/co-op

Infrastructure Business Operations Support (IBOS) is seeking an experienced Logistics Operations Lead to own New Product Introduction (NPI) and lab support across NORAM field logistics. The Logistics Operations Lead is the primary liaison between Hardware Engineering, field operations teams, and supply chain partners during product ramps — proving out receiving, staging, storage, kitting, and distribution flows for products that have never moved through the network before, then hardening and standardizing those flows for scale. In this role, you will drive asset tracking, inventory control, audit execution, and disposition strategies that support Meta's data centers, offices, and technical facilities. You will partner with cross-functional teams including procurement, finance, IT, and facilities to ensure asset data integrity, compliance with internal controls, and operational efficiency across the full asset lifecycle from acquisition through retirement.

Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with cross-functional partners including Data Center Site Operations, Sourcing, Accounting, Finance, SOX compliance, Trade Compliance, and Tax to develop and oversee asset management business processes in a global environment
  • Execute physical and logical audits of Meta's infrastructure asset base, conducting fieldwork including observations, assessments, and control testing to identify and document findings such as deficiencies and areas for improvement
  • Domestic and International Travel is a requirement 25%-30%
  • Identify and assess ongoing and emerging risks within asset management operations, developing approaches to resolve technical problems and building short- and long-term roadmaps aligned to business and operational needs
  • Develop and maintain audit plans and checklists to ensure comprehensive asset coverage, and present findings with corrective recommendations to stakeholders
  • Develop and improve decentralized policies, standards, processes, workflows, and controls to support emerging operational requirements with a focus on accountability, standardization, scale, and efficiency
  • Conduct design reviews of proposed automation and process improvements against business goals, operations governance, data integrity, and compliance requirements
  • Establish and monitor KPIs to measure asset management process performance and identify continuous improvement opportunities
  • Maintain data integrity across multiple asset management and ERP systems, identify root causes of data inconsistencies, and leverage data insights to surface new operational requirements
  • Develop process documentation for implementation and rollout of asset management business process improvements
  • Support implementation of broader technology solutions and process automation to advance asset lifecycle tracking and inventory reconciliation at scale

Minimum Qualifications

  • 6+ years of experience in asset management, supply chain operations, or technical logistics within large-scale IT or facilities environments
  • Experience managing physical and IT asset lifecycles including tagging, tracking, auditing, and disposition processes
  • Experience with enterprise asset management or ERP systems such as ServiceNow, Oracle, or SAP for inventory tracking and financial reconciliation
  • Experience developing and enforcing inventory control procedures and supporting Sarbanes-Oxley or equivalent compliance requirements
  • Experience using data analysis tools to monitor asset inventory metrics, identify discrepancies, and drive operational decisions

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience integrating AI tools or automation into asset tracking and inventory reconciliation workflows to drive measurable efficiency gains
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Familiarity with IT asset disposition standards, including data sanitization, remarketing, and environmentally responsible recycling practices
  • Experience managing asset operations across data center or large-scale technical site environments, including third-party logistics or asset management vendor oversight
  • IAITAM or ITIL certification, or equivalent professional credential in asset or service management
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Brand Insights, Measurement Lead at Anthropic, you will strengthen the evidence that fuels our brand decisions: knowing whether marketing spend and effort is working, saying so clearly on a schedule to the people who need to hear it. Marketing Insights turns market, campaign and user data into decisions that product, marketing, comms and sales leadership can act on. You'll tell us, with data, whether awareness is turning into consideration, whether consideration is turning into pipeline, and where that chain breaks down for a given audience. This role sits at the intersection of human understanding, marketing science discipline and organizational influence.

In this role, you'll own the team's recurring measurement readouts, including the Prosumer and B2B brand health tracker studies and the metrics, headwinds and tailwinds that show up in front of business leadership and in all-hands updates, keeping them accurate, current and easy to act on. You'll partner closely with your Marketing Insights teammates, Comms and data science on the brand-health dashboard, Brand & Integrated Marketing leadership, brand data science, research vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders across Enterprise Marketing, product marketing and finance.

Responsibilities

  • Own the recurring executive and all-hands readouts that put key metrics, headwinds and tailwinds in front of marketing management and the broader team
  • Lead process ownership of the Prosumer and B2B brand health tracker studies, including managing the research vendor relationships that field them
  • Lead coordination across Comms, Marketing and data science on the brand-health dashboard, aligning all three groups on one consistent view of the data
  • Support media mix modeling, multi-touch attribution and incrementality analyses that inform how marketing budget and effort get allocated, moving the team past correlation to a defensible read on what's actually driving outcomes
  • Run best-practice pre- and post-campaign analysis on individual campaigns, covering creative, channel, audience, and timing effects, and turn each read into a specific change for the next campaign
  • Roll up campaign-level learnings into a recurring view for leadership: which channels, creative approaches, and audiences are outperforming over time, and where the team should adjust the playbook next
  • Build audience and funnel analyses that quantify how different audiences move, and relate to each other, from awareness through consideration to conversion, and what that means for where to invest
  • Audit how customer sentiment gets reported across the business and design a more efficient, consistent process
  • Manage the underlying data pipelines so that recurring readouts stay reliable and don't get rebuilt from scratch each cycle
  • Partner with Marketing Insights teammates to keep measurement process and research design in sync, including feeding into the Marketing Business Review scorecard process
  • Develop one defensible view from first-party behavioral data, campaign and media data, and survey or attitudinal research, being clear about what each source can and can't tell you on its own
  • Present findings to non-technical audiences, including marketing leadership, enterprise sales and finance partners, translating hedged results into clear recommendations

You may be a good fit if you

  • Have a strategic orientation, strong curiosity for understanding what customers and users think and how to shift perceptions, and can use that to influence business and marketing direction
  • Are fluent in SQL and Python or R, and move comfortably between a quick exploratory pull and a more rigorous statistical model
  • Have designed or analyzed experiments (A/B tests, holdouts, lift tests) to establish a causal effect rather than settle for a correlation, and have applied regression, segmentation or other causal-inference methods to a real business question
  • Have run campaign-level measurement end to end, from a pre/post read on a single campaign to synthesizing learnings across multiple campaigns into a change the team acts on next time
  • Have built and maintained a recurring metrics report or dashboard that executives or cross-functional partners actually rely on, and kept it trustworthy over time
  • Can turn a hedged, caveated finding into a clear recommendation a non-technical stakeholder can act on, and know which caveat matters enough to keep in the headline
  • Start an analysis by pinning down the business question and the decision it needs to serve, not the method that's most interesting to run
  • Can reconcile data with no universal taxonomy across first-party, third-party, real-time and survey sources
  • Know when a directionally correct answer now beats a more rigorous one that arrives too late to matter
  • Work well across functions, building credibility with both technical partners and non-technical leadership
  • Are excited about Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial

Strong candidates may also have

  • Experience with media mix modeling, multi-touch attribution or incrementality and lift testing specifically, rather than general-purpose analytics
  • Experience advising marketing stakeholders on experimental design for live campaigns (email, paid social), or measuring marketing performance across multiple markets
  • Familiarity with survey-based quantitative research (MaxDiff, conjoint, brand and sentiment tracking) alongside behavioral and usage data
  • Experience with a modern data warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery) and a BI tool (Tableau, Looker, Power BI)
  • Prior experience in marketing, growth or brand analytics specifically, rather than data science in a general or product context
  • A graduate degree in statistics, economics or another quantitative field
  • A career trajectory spanning BI and dashboarding, applied causal inference and experimental design, and multi-market marketing measurement

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Your job is to develop and curate the right material on a rapid cadence,   and to tailor content for each audience, ensuring that the messages, formats, and channels each cloud uses to upskill their sellers and solutions architects can position and deploy Claude with confidence. Land our mission and differentiation. You'll make sure Anthropic's mission and our approach to safe, responsible frontier AI show up accurately and consistently wherever cloud sellers encounter us, so the case for Anthropic as the enterprise's trusted AI partner is clear. Ensure internal and external readiness. You'll shape our certifications and scaled training for the way each cloud learns and upskills its people. Connect the field to the content. You'll pair internal assets with what our GTM team are hearing in customer conversations, and turn that traction into co-sell plays and assets the next hundred sellers can use without anyone from our team in the room.

Measuring Impact. You'll define the signals that connect this work to partner-sourced pipeline, deal velocity, and seller engagement, watch what's actually changing seller behavior, and adjust based on what you see.

  • The ability to influence people you don't manage, across Anthropic and inside large partner organizations
  • Willingness to dive in and figure out what needs to be done, often without concrete guidance or a large supporting team

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.

We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in Louisiana to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centers are sited, built, and operated. This is not a communications role or a government affairs role, though you will do elements of both. It is a relationship role: your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbor, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.

You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.

You will travel regularly within Louisiana, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data center markets.

Key responsibilities

  • Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with parish presidents and councils, police juries, mayors and municipal officials, parish planning and zoning bodies, port, levee, and drainage districts, state economic development agencies, community groups, civic leaders, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the Louisiana data center markets you cover

  • Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations

  • Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate

  • Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media

  • Monitor community sentiment and local political dynamics, and advise internal teams on risks, opportunities, and the right pace and posture for engagement

  • Partner with the Real Estate and Infrastructure team to bring community input into how projects are planned, communicated, and delivered, not just how they are announced

  • Work with the Communications team to develop proactive, locally relevant messaging

  • Coordinate charitable giving, community investment, and economic development commitments in your markets, including managing nonprofit partner relationships

  • Partner with the Energy and Sustainability team to explain our approach to environmental stewardship and respond to questions about power, water, and land use, including flood risk, storm resilience, and how large electricity needs are served by local utilities

  • Build a community engagement playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience in community affairs, public affairs, economic development, government relations, local or state government, or a closely related field

  • Direct experience working for or engaging with parish and municipal governments and a broad set of community stakeholders on behalf of large infrastructure, construction, energy, or technology projects, with a working understanding of how local politics and community dynamics actually play out

  • A skilled relationship and coalition builder who earns trust with a diverse group of stakeholders, and who maintains relationships through difficult conversations

  • The ability to represent a company credibly in public settings, including town halls, hearings, and press interviews

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to turn a complex operational plan into plain language that a local official or reporter can understand and respond to

  • The ability to work independently, get up to speed quickly on complex policy issues, and manage multiple concurrent engagements across different markets without losing track of any of them

  • Based in Louisiana or willing to relocate there, and prepared to travel regularly across the state

Preferred qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in community engagement specifically on data center, utility, energy, or large-scale industrial infrastructure projects, or in local government

  • Familiarity with land use, zoning, and permitting processes at the parish and municipal level, including local review of industrial tax incentives

  • Experience in communities with a long industrial, energy, or port presence, and an understanding of coastal, flood, and hurricane resilience concerns

  • Experience managing corporate social responsibility programs

  • Established relationships with economic development, workforce, or civic organizations in the markets this role covers

  • Experience working with real estate, legal, communications, and policy teams at the same time

  • Experience engaging with Tribal nations in Louisiana, including familiarity with consultation processes and Tribal sovereignty

  • A genuine interest in the communities where you work, not just the projects you are managing
