Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maneuver Dominance team at Anduril develops operationally relevant, multi-asset autonomy. We are focused on new air vehicle development programs, and making large groups of autonomous systems work effectively together. 

Within the Maneuver Dominance team, we are growing an early-stage, undisclosed autonomous air vehicle (AAV) program at our Costa Mesa HQ. This team is chartered with re-inventing an existing platform through heavy modification and integration of advanced autonomy, mission systems, and payloads. 

On this team, you will be tackling novel challenges across airframe, structures, avionics, and software from day one. As part of this program, you'll work alongside a tight-knit group of mechanical, structural, electrical, and software engineers, together with Program Leads and the Chief Engineer, all embedded in a single team driving toward major milestones.

You will work in a lean, high-ownership culture where the entire vehicle team sits side-by-side, iterating quickly and making decisions in real time. Given the early stage of the program, you will have influence over foundational architecture decisions and the opportunity to redefine an existing platform.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking a Lead Air Vehicle Engineer to join the Maneuver Dominance team at our Costa Mesa HQ to lead the convergence of technical efforts in developing an advanced airborne platform. This individual will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of vertical flight focusing on air vehicle development and integrating mission autonomy to meet the evolving demands of defense capabilities.

Here you will work on core product development for unmanned rotorcraft and complex systems, including but not limited to aircraft configuration, composites, mechanisms, and structures. The role requires high ownership and frequent collaboration with other core disciplines. The ideal candidate would be practical, hands-on, and a self starter. High growth potential is possible as well as additional leadership opportunities.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Execute rapid evaluation of engineering concepts across a wide range of aerospace disciplines
  • Perform trade studies and physics-based analysis of blue-sky engineering problems
  • Advanced design, configuration, implementation of a highly complex advanced air vehicle
  • Operate with extreme visibility and exercise a vast level of professional autonomy
  • Lead design reviews, run analysis, interface with vendors, define and execute hardware test plans
  • Build prototypes, analyze failures, and transition successful projects into production
  • Support critical software and hardware demonstrations with customers as needed
  • Use first principles physics as a basis for every decision
  • Ability to provide input across a variety of technical domains not limited to: aerodynamics, flight dynamics, GNC, aeroelastic, loads and dynamics

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Physics , or related technical discipline.
  • Minimum of 8 years in technical leadership roles such as Technical Program Manager, Chief Engineer, Lead Engineer, or similarly relevant position.
  • Leadership experience in engineering team management and project execution for aerospace or defense sectors.
  • Deep experience developing VTOL platforms.
  • Broad exposure to aircraft concepts, design layouts, static stability, control architectures and propulsion concepts.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire cross-functional teams, fostering a collaborative environment that drives innovation and project success.
  • Strong project management skills, with experience using tools like JIRA and Confluence, and knowledge of Agile and Waterfall methodologies.
  • Exceptional communication and stakeholder management abilities, capable of engaging effectively with both technical teams and non-technical partners.
  • Knowledge of aircraft design principles, including familiarity with vertical lift, as well as aircraft build and integration, and flight test execution/oversight.
  • Hands-on experience with the development and deployment of autonomous systems, particularly in rotorcraft or large UAS.
  • Eligible to obtain a U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Ability to travel up to 50% depending on the product lifecycle

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct experience with autonomous systems, specifically with the development and integration of rotorcraft or larger UAS.
  • Deep familiarity with unmanned aircraft, autonomous systems, robotics, aircraft design.
  • Knowledgeable in the nuanced integration of complex systems, such as launched effects, into aerial platforms, ensuring system compatibility and performance.
  • An extensive network within the aerospace industry, enabling effective collaboration and leveraging partnerships for product development.
  • Familiarity with Defense Acquisition Processes and a clear understanding of key review stages and compliance requirements.
  • Relevant professional certifications that underscore a commitment to continuous learning and application of industry best practices.
  • Customer-facing experience with a proven ability to lead high-profile programs and navigate complex client relationships with confidence and authority.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Special Access Program Security team is responsible for ensuring the security of classified information for Anduril’s most sensitive programs and contracts. The team has individuals located across the country and works in a collaborative manner to ensure the security of Anduril and government information, and Anduril’s defense products.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Contractor Special Access Program Security Officer (CSSO) to join our growing team in Washington, DC. This is a security position requiring a qualified security professional in support of special access program initiatives. As a CSSO, you will be responsible for the management, direction, administration and development of security programs and procedures for assigned programs that have contractually imposed security requirements beyond 32 CFR Part 117, National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM) Rule requirements to include DoDM 5205.07, Intelligence Community Directives (ICDs 703, 704, 505, and others as applicable), Security Classification Guides (SCGs), and Statements of Work. Key responsibilities include Personnel Security, Physical Security and program OPSEC/Program Protection planning. The CSSO will interface with government agencies regarding assigned program security matters and requirements and will be responsible for managing all security-related aspects of assigned programs in close collaboration with other Anduril CSSOs. This will require detailed knowledge of the government policies applicable to Special Access Program (SAP) security, as well as practical experience implementing this knowledge to a fast-paced, quickly scaling, and complex manufacturing environment. If you are someone who enjoys fast-paced and collaborative work, finding solutions to interesting challenges, and possess a “can do” attitude, then this role is for you!

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Knowledgeable in interpreting and implementing security guidance based on applicable ICDs, SEADs, 32 CFR Part 117. “NISPOM Rule,” DoDM 5205.07, and other policies, regulations, and processes as applicable.
  • Perform all aspects of Customer Personnel Security Program requirements. This includes, guidance and assistance for validation of SAP access, access requirements, processing and eligibility and polygraph requests, nomination interviews, submission of investigative requests, and conducting SAP security briefings.
  • Perform all aspects of Physical Security by providing day to day support for badging, access control and visitor control. Ensure all SCIF/SAP Facility documentation is current and up to date.
  • Support program managers and personnel with classification guidance and other program related requirements, i.e., incoming and outgoing visit certifications, foreign travel reporting and proposal support.
  • Ensure SAP material is properly controlled, transmitted, transported, packaged, safeguarded, and destroyed, as appropriate.
  • Investigate security incidents and prepare required reports.
  • Build and maintain a relationship with government security counterparts.
  • Provide security awareness training as required by regulations and as requested by our customers.
  • Work with IT and ISSO to ensure equipment being brought into the secure areas is authorized and approved.
  • Assist and provide guidance on ICD 705 modifications/upgrades at company site(s).
  • Collaborate and assist the ISSO / ISSM on management of information systems.
  • Maintain personnel security records for special access programs to include the use of SIMS, DISS, JADE, and other systems as applicable.
  • Conduct internal self-inspections and manage government Staff Assistance Visits and Customer Security Assessments on behalf of Anduril.
  • Maintain classified material accountability records to include inventory lists, receipt and transmittal records and final disposition documentation.
  • Maintain working knowledge in the preparation and maintenance of prime and subcontract DD254s.
  • Develop and maintain the program's Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).
  • In collaboration with the physical security team, maintain the program’s access control and alarm systems.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in related discipline or equivalent education and work experience.
  • At least four years’ experience working with special programs in a ACSSO or CSSO role.
  • Ability to work independently and possess knowledge over the full range of security principles, including but not limited to identifying and evaluating program risks/vulnerability; implementing mitigating improvement; and disseminating security procedures/processes.
  • Build and maintain relationships with government security counterparts.
  • DoD Top Secret clearance with SCI eligibility with current investigation and ability to maintain a DoD Top Secret clearance with Special Program accesses.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Willing to work extended hours in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment in a variety of program areas.
  • Willingness to travel on company business (varies but probably less than 15%).

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Global Defense (GD) team is responsible for establishing and expanding Anduril's international business, developing and delivering the products and technology that address the unique security challenges faced by America's Allies and partners. The team operates across every major theater, pairing deep regional expertise with a sophisticated command of foreign military sales, trade, and compliance frameworks.

GD team members serve as the bridge between international customers and the broader Anduril enterprise; they translate partner-nation requirements and perspectives back to Anduril's Business Lines, while serving as Anduril's ambassadors and partners abroad. They shape and capture new opportunities by leveraging Anduril's strengths in innovation, modern warfighting, agile foreign sales strategies, and rigorous export compliance. The team's work spans the full lifecycle of international engagement: global strategy and market analysis; international business development and deal navigation; partnerships and representation; trade, export control, and Tech Security & Foreign Disclosure (TSFD); and the global operations, security, and in-country presence required to execute.

The Director, Mission Insights, Maritime sits within Global Defense Mission Operations and brings deep maritime operational expertise to Anduril's international pursuits. You will be the operator voice in the room with partner navies, with an initial focus on supporting Anduril's maritime pursuit in Japan, translating mission needs into credible concepts of operation and product requirements.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Define Allied Maritime CONEMPs: Develop authoritative reference missions, operational vignettes, tactics, techniques, and procedures, and concepts of employment tailored to partner-nation maritime forces (e.g., long range strike in the Indo-Pacific, Baltic grey-zone incursions, Strait of Hormuz chokepoint security).
  • Feed Realities into Engineering & Business Lines: Act as the direct conduit between allied maritime operators and Anduril’s engineering and product teams. Ensure real-world operational constraints (e.g., degraded RF/bandwidth environments, specific sea-state realities, sovereign sensor networks) are baked into product design and R&D pipelines.
  • Support Operational Analysis & Objective "Red Teaming": Provide threat-informed and rigorous analysis on concepts of employment to support Anduril’s operational analysis teams. Rigorously evaluate how Anduril hardware and software perform in allied scenarios versus existing competitor or legacy architectures.
  • Enable Global Growth & Capture: Arm regional Business Development leads with high-impact sales enablement tools, including localized wargaming outcomes, cost-exchange analyses, and mission architectures that clearly articulate mission viability to foreign defense leaders.
  • Bridge Interoperability Architectures: Define the mission frameworks necessary for allied sovereign maritime systems to seamlessly interoperate with US JADC2 networks, FVEY, and NATO tactical standards.
  • Seed Net-New Capabilities: Identify genuine capability gaps in allied naval forces to pitch, shape, and seed requirements for international co-development projects or net-new Anduril US production lines.
  • Translate Strategy to Execution: Act as a polished, credible operational lead in front of international military leaders, ministries of defense, and cross-functional internal stakeholders during capture shaping and proposal stages.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Former U.S. Navy Surface Warfare Officer (SWO) with operational experience at sea.
  • Designation as a Weapons and Tactics Instructor (WTI) via the Surface and Mine Warfighting Development Center (SMWDC) or equivalent high-end tactical instructor tour.
  • Deep expertise in maritime warfighting scenarios, multi-domain integration, surface warfare, integrated air and missile defense (IAMD), or mine countermeasures (MCM).
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex tactical and technical problems into concise, compelling operational concepts for senior military and civilian executives.
  • Exceptional public speaking, briefing, and technical writing skills; comfortable engaging directly with foreign flag-level officers and government defense officials.
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time, both domestically and internationally.
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Previous operational planning experience (N3/N5 or J3/J5) at USPACFLT, USINDOPACOM, or a Forward Deployed Naval Forces staff.
  • Familiarity with allied naval concepts of operations and interoperability dynamics across the Indo-Pacific.
  • Background in operations research, operational analysis, wargaming, or modeling and simulation tools.
  • Familiarity with autonomous maritime systems (USVs, UUVs), uncrewed distributed sensors, edge-compute networks, and command-and-control (C2) software.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a technical, engineering, or national security field; advanced degree preferred.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret SCI security clearance

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maneuver Dominance team at Anduril develops operationally relevant, multi-asset autonomy. We are focused on new air vehicle development programs, and making large groups of autonomous systems work effectively together. 

Within the Maneuver Dominance team, we are growing an early-stage, undisclosed autonomous air vehicle (AAV) program at our Costa Mesa HQ. This team is chartered with re-inventing an existing platform through heavy modification and integration of advanced autonomy, mission systems, and payloads. 

On this team, you will be tackling novel challenges across airframe, structures, avionics, and software from day one. As part of this program, you'll work alongside a tight-knit group of mechanical, structural, electrical, and software engineers, together with Program Leads and the Chief Engineer, all embedded in a single team driving toward major milestones.

You will work in a lean, high-ownership culture where the entire vehicle team sits side-by-side, iterating quickly and making decisions in real time. Given the early stage of the program, you will have influence over foundational architecture decisions and the opportunity to redefine an existing platform.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

In this position, you will work closely with the program leadership and a wide spectrum of cross-departments as part of a team focused on solving hard problems and changing the industry forever. In this role you will be responsible for designing and supporting the integration of various subsystems, supporting testing efforts, and ensuring overall system performance meets the required specifications and standards. Join our dynamic team and help us build the next generation of autonomous flight systems.

  • Full cycle aircraft systems electrical design and integration including requirements capture, system architecture design, equipment selection, supervision or completion of wire harness build, bring-up, test, and rework.
  • Troubleshoot issues that span the electrical and software boundaries, with solid skills using both lab equipment (Oscilloscopes, DMM, etc.) and basic software debugging tools
  • Development of payloads and subsystems (sensors, payload interfaces, power management, and networking)
  • Develop system interconnect diagrams and define wire harnesses that connect electronic equipment within a subsystem
  • Work closely with other electrical, mechanical, software, firmware, and test engineers to deliver fully functional products
  • Work in a fast-paced environment supporting new developments and customer operated hardware
  • Conduct peer-level and cross-discipline design reviews
  • Design and support the integration & testing of an rotorcraft system through TRLs 3-8
  • Conduct vehicle platform system design & analysis as required by your supported program or effort
  • Conduct design reviews, perform requirements analysis, and plan system verification to ensure compliance with project goals and industry standards
  • Work within a dynamic team of multidisciplinary engineers and specialists throughout the life of product design, integration, and test effort

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent
  • 3+ years of experience (non-internship) designing, testing, and troubleshooting complex board designs
  • Knowledge of modern analog and digital electronics and electronic circuits
  • Competence with test equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, thermal chambers, current-probes, and automation of tests
  • Familiarity with standard interfaces such as Ethernet, CAN, I2C, SPI, PCIe, USB, etc.
  • Familiarity with common MCU, CPU, FPGA devices and technologies
  • Familiarity with software development processes and tools such as git, Github, JIRA, etc
  • Comfortable with a variety of electronic CAD tools (Altium preferred, Eagle and others acceptable)
  • Experience in design for signal integrity / power integrity
  • Experience with battery systems and ability to support alternate battery systems design
  • Experience with high reliability systems
  • Experience with radio frequency-based systems
  • Experience with rapid payload/sensor integration
  • Experience in designing and integrating high power electronics
  • Experience in fieldable system design
  • Comfortable in conducting worst case circuit or uncertainty analysis
  • High-ownership and a bias toward action – if you see a problem, you want to solve and fix it
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Ability to travel 25% with potential surges above 25%

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience designing electrical and power systems for autonomous rotorcraft
  • Experience with battery systems both primary and secondary chemistries
  • Experience with High Voltage Power Electronics
  • Experience with inverters and high power electric motors
  • Understanding of MIL-STD-461, MIL-STD-810G
  • Outstanding leadership and interpersonal skills
  • Familiarity with running a qualification campaign for flight hardware
  • Familiarity with designing for rugged environments
  • Experience with electro-mechanical and electrical design concepts
  • Experience with Formula SAE, Baja SAE, Design Build Fly, etc.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Air Dominance & Strike Electromechanical Engineers are responsible for the mechanical packaging, interconnect architecture, and structural integration of avionics, power systems, and electro-optical payloads across Group 5 aircrafts and our high-speed missiles. The team owns the full development lifecycle—from concept through qualification and flight operations—delivering rugged, high-performance electromechanical systems optimized for Size, Weight, Power, and Cost (SWaP-C).

WHAT YOU'LL DO
  • Design flight-critical enclosures, chassis, and mechanical packaging for high-density circuit card assemblies, battery systems, electro-optical payloads, and cable/harness assemblies.
  • Collaborate with electrical engineers to inform PCBA layout, define connector configurations, manage keep-out zones, route harnesses, and establish thermal and grounding interfaces.
  • Create detailed 3D models, drawing packages, and GD&T and tolerance stack-up analyses to ensure designs are optimized for assembly, serviceability, and high-yield manufacturing.
  • Conduct hand calculations and structural FEA, working with thermal and fatigue analysts to validate performance before committing to physical hardware.
  • Design hardware to survive aerospace environments—vibration, shock, thermal extremes, moisture, and EMI/EMC—meeting standards such as MIL-STD-810, MIL-STD-464/461, and DO-160.
  • Lead root-cause investigations and corrective actions for mechanical, environmental, or manufacturing anomalies found during qualification or flight operations.
  • Support design reviews (PDR/CDR) and drive execution of engineering deliverables across distributed, cross-functional teams including systems, hardware, software, manufacturing, test, and supply chain.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • B.S. or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Aerospace Engineering, or equivalent experience.
  • 4+ years of experience in electronics packaging and/or electromechanical systems design in aerospace, defense, automotive, or robotics.
  • Direct experience designing hardware to MIL-STD-810 and MIL-STD-464/461 environmental and EMI/EMC standards.
  • Proficiency with 3D CAD (Siemens NX, SolidWorks, CATIA, or similar) for complex surface modeling, enclosure packaging, and harness routing.
  • Understanding of advanced manufacturing processes including CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, casting, injection molding, and 3D printing, with hands-on prototyping experience.
  • Strong communication, collaboration, and teamwork skills across multi-site, multi-disciplinary teams.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • Extensive experience with Siemens NX and Teamcenter.
  • Familiarity with eCAD tools (Altium, Cadence Allegro) and harness design software (Siemens Capital, Zuken E3).
  • Practical understanding of bare-board PCB manufacturing, high-density interconnect (HDI) stackups, and SMT assembly standards (IPC-A-610/J-STD-001).
  • Advanced FEA and thermal simulation experience with tools such as Ansys Mechanical, Ansys Icepak, FloTHERM, or Ansys Sherlock.
  • Experience designing battery modules/packs or precision-aligned electro-optical/sensor payloads.
  • Active Top Secret DoD clearance.

The Rocket Motor Systems (RMS) team at Anduril designs and manufactures solid rocket motors and propulsion systems for the next generation of missiles and munitions. RMS runs a vertically integrated energetics operation - from propellant chemistry and mixing through case fabrication, assembly, and test. We move fast in a highly regulated, safety-critical environment, and we depend on accurate, real-time inventory to keep production lines building.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Inventory Analyst is responsible for managing and optimizing inventory levels to support production schedules while minimizing the costs of scrap, excess and obsolescence. This role will oversee the health of inventory across materials, quality, and production - including energetic and shelf-life-sensitive chemicals unique to a rocket motor environment. The candidate will analyze usage trends, lead cycle counting programs, monitor variances and resolve discrepancies to ensure inventory integrity in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Oversee electronic cycle counts and physical audits to maintain near-perfect record accuracy.
  • Investigate root causes of inventory variances and implement corrective actions in our ERP and WMS systems.
  • Monitor shelf-life-sensitive materials and ensure compliance with safety and quality storage regulations via the AS9100 Quality Management System.
  • Generate KPI reports and visual dashboards to track inventory health, aging stock, and transaction records.
  • Collaborate with other manufacturing stakeholders to support operational continuity and efficient forecasting and planning.
  • Track shelf-life and expiration on energetic and hazardous materials - ammonium perchlorate (AP), propellant chemicals, and controlled CHM-coded consumables - and flag lots approaching removal, repack, or retest dates before they impact the line.
  • Reconcile physical counts to the system of record (Odoo/Oracle), measure count accuracy against the fiscal-year target, and drive root-cause corrections on adjustments.
  • Analyze consumption trends and clear-to-build coverage against active work orders to surface shortages and long-lead risk before they block production.
  • Monitor MRB and quarantine aging, dormant and dead stock, and warehouse capacity utilization, and recommend disposition or consolidation.
  • Validate inventory striped to the correct project and task charge codes, and flag material at risk from expired project dates.
  • Build and maintain self-service dashboards and reports that give production, quality, and program teams a live view of inventory health.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Data Science or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
  • Typically 3-5+ years in inventory control within an aerospace or high-tech manufacturing environment.
  • Proficiency in Oracle and Odoo (highly preferred), advanced Excel (PivotTables, VLOOKUPs), and potentially SQL for data mining.
  • Familiarity with AS9100 standards and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) regulations for the management of government property.
  • Experience managing parts with unique serial numbers or traceability requirements, where a single error can halt production.
  • Experience identifying inefficiencies in material flow and driving Lean or Six Sigma initiatives to improve them.
  • Comfort handling data on hazardous or energetic materials with strict segregation, storage, and shelf-life requirements. Familiarity with hazmat or magazine storage is a plus.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in a defense, aerospace, propulsion, or energetics manufacturing environment.
  • Hands-on experience building dashboards or reports from ERP data (Odoo, Oracle) or a BI/analytics platform.
  • Familiarity with Oracle project and task charge structures and inventory project striping.
  • Track record of improving inventory KPIs - count accuracy, aging, putaway lead time, capacity utilization, on-time kitting.

$86,000—$112,000 USD

Our IT Asset Management (ITAM) team is the backbone of our corporate technology operations. We manage the full lifecycle of every endpoint asset, from receiving in our facility to secure, eco-friendly disposal. We combine software automation, precise inventory auditing, and streamlined physical logistics so our workforce always has the tools it needs. We are a collaborative, detail-oriented group that connects high-level vendor compliance with hands-on, day-to-day technical support. On our team, you will play a critical role in keeping our global IT endpoint devices organized, cost-effective, and ready to scale.

ABOUT THE JOB
We are seeking an IT Asset Management Technician I to primarily support our offboarding and asset recovery program. You will own the day-to-day returns workflow for departing employees, contractors, and interns: making sure every device is recovered, verified, secured, and returned to service quickly. You will also support IT audit assessments that keep our asset records accurate. When the team needs extra hands, you will help with inventory and deployments. You will work closely with our Asset Administrator, People Business Partners, managers, and regional IT teams.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Offboarding & Returns

  • Departure Coordination: Manage offboarding cases from start to finish. Confirm each leaver's assigned devices, set the return method and location, and keep stakeholders updated until every device is back.
  • Return Logistics: Issue return shipping labels and QR codes, arrange return boxes, track shipments, and follow up on unreturned devices according to our escalation timelines.
  • Receiving & Verification: Receive returned devices, verify serial numbers against the asset record, and update the asset management system the same day.
  • Data & Device Security: Follow data-preservation and legal-hold procedures, including device imaging when required, before devices are wiped, released, and returned to inventory.
  • Return Tracking: Keep the return tracker current on a regular cadence, close out completed cases, and report outstanding devices and trends.
  • Volume Surges: Support high-volume events, such as intern cohort departures and refresh programs, with clear organization and steady follow-through.

Auditing

  • Record Accuracy: Run recurring audits to confirm the assigned user, owner, and location of each device are correct in our asset management system, and cross-check against other data sources.
  • Discrepancy Investigation: Investigate mismatches, such as unreturned devices, users with more than one computer that goes unused, and shared or service devices without a named owner. Resolve each one or escalate it.
  • User Verification: Support user device confirmations and document results so they are ready for compliance reviews.

Inventory & Deployment Support (as needed)

  • Physical Logistics: Move, stock, and deploy inventory (must be able to lift up to 50 lbs). This includes moving pallets, breaking down boxes, and stocking shelves.
  • Device Maintenance: Physically clean and wipe returned assets, and partner with cross-functional teams on repairs and RMA (Return Merchandise Authorization) processes so devices are ready to redeploy.
  • Workspace Setup: Set up desks, monitors, and peripherals for new hires and team moves when needed.
  • Support Ticket Resolution: Handle offboarding and returns tickets in Jira and walk-up requests, and provide deskside support as needed.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Soft Skills: Eager, motivated, collaborative, reliable, and highly customer-focused, with professional, tactful communication when working with departing team members and their managers.
  • Organization & Follow-Through: Able to manage many open cases at once, track deadlines, and follow up consistently until each case is closed.
  • Attention to Detail: This role focuses heavily on verifying serial numbers and matching records, so strong attention to detail is essential.
  • Inventory Control: Experience maintaining accurate inventory counts and asset records.
  • Discretion: Comfortable handling sensitive situations and data, including involuntary separations and legal holds, with confidentiality.
  • Physical Capability: Comfortable with physical labor, standing or walking for most of the day, and lifting heavy items (50 lbs+).
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a US Secret Security Clearance.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Connected Warfare division builds systems to support global command and control missions. We create joint, time-sensitive, multi-domain, ubiquitous, connected mesh ecosystems. Our technology enables connected warfare with disproportional impact by connecting every robot, human, and sensor in every domain, bringing together hundreds of thousands of endpoints across the globe. We are the substrate that provides the source of truth for time-sensitive decisions, effectively transforming the way that militaries close kill chains and enable mission autonomy.

The Mission Operations (MOPs) team is responsible for managing the execution, growth, and success of our customer accounts. Based out of our regional hub in the UAE, our team owns customer relationships across the GCC. We work side-by-side with operators to deploy our Connected Warfare products in support of their missions. Because the problems we solve are uniquely challenging, our team members naturally gravitate toward finding solutions, navigating hurdles, and doing whatever it takes to ensure mission success.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking an ambitious, hands-on Mission Operations Specialist to lead the deployment, user training, and day-to-day operational success of our Connected Warfare products in Kuwait.

Based out of our UAE office, you will be the primary technical and operational bridge to our Kuwaiti defense and national security customers. This is not a desk job. You will be on the ground in Kuwait up to 50% of the time, working directly with end-users, setting up tactical mesh networks, integrating sensors, and ensuring our command and control (C2) software performs flawlessly in the field. 

This is an execution-focused role designed for a highly capable, technically minded professional ready to take immense ownership of a key GCC defense account.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Orchestrate Tactical Deployments: Lead the physical deployment and configuration of our Connected Warfare hardware, software, and sensor networks in support of Kuwaiti customer missions.
  • Train the Operator: Design and deliver hands-on training to military, security, and tactical operators, ensuring they are fully capable of utilizing our mesh networks and C2 systems.
  • Bridge the Gap to Engineering: Work side-by-side with users in the field to understand their specific workflow challenges, translating real-world operational requirements back to our engineering teams in the UAE and globally.
  • Drive Local Account Success: Build trust-based relationships with mid-level officers and technical stakeholders in Kuwait to ensure high system adoption and uncover future mission needs.
  • Cross-Functional Execution: Coordinate with UAE-based logistics, legal, and engineering teams to ensure deployments in Kuwait are executed seamlessly and meet strict timelines.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

  • Mission-First Mindset: You put the needs of the customer and the mission first. You are motivated by the opportunity to radically evolve national and international defense capabilities.
  • Extreme Ownership: We look for owners. You will be entrusted with high levels of responsibility in Kuwait. You must be comfortable stepping up, solving vague technical problems, and driving tasks to completion on the ground without constant supervision.
  • Technical & Tactical Aptitude: We are first and foremost a deep-tech company working with machine learning, distributed networking, and sensor fusion. You must have a strong desire to understand how complex hardware/software systems operate and be comfortable troubleshooting them in high-pressure field environments.
  • Collaboration & Adaptability: You thrive in unstructured environments and enjoy working as part of a flat, low-ego, fast-moving team that values teamwork over hierarchy.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Serve in a customer-facing capacity, working directly with Kuwaiti defense/security entities to deploy Connected Warfare products.
  • Own the delivery of operational contracts, including system setups, performance monitoring, and creating user engagement roadmaps.
  • Design and implement user feedback loops to gather, triage, and prioritize requirements and software bugs found during field use or training exercises.
  • Provide direct input to product development teams to drive features that enhance user workflows and operational efficiency.
  • Travel frequently between the UAE and Kuwait (up to 50% travel) to support active operations, field testing, and training events.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Prior experience in field operations, technical deployment, defense technology, tactical communications, systems integration, or technical customer success roles.
  • Strong technical aptitude with a proven ability to troubleshoot hardware, software, and basic IP networking/RF communications in the field.
  • Outstanding interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build rapport with tactical operators and technical teams.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.
  • Based in the UAE (or willing to relocate) with a passport/visa status that allows for rapid, seamless travel to Kuwait.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain necessary local security clearances required for Kuwaiti military and government installations.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Academic background in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related technical field.
  • Prior experience or familiarity with military operations, C2 (Command & Control) systems, intelligence workflows, or unmanned systems.
  • Experience configuring or troubleshooting tactical networks, sensors, or edge-computing devices.

ABOUT THE TEAM

  • Anduril's Reliability & System Safety Engineering organization is hiring Principal System Safety Engineers to operate across the entire company. This role is not scoped to a single program or product line. Domains include Air Dominance & Strike, Maritime, Ground Systems, Space, Counter-UAS, and Autonomy/Lattice. The Reliability & System Safety Engineering team works with our broader Engineering team to ensure our products are safe and meet all mission performance, environmental, and customer requirements. We develop cutting-edge System Safety processes and methods to secure scalable, long-term business success.
  • As a Principal System Safety Engineer at Anduril, you are a company-wide technical authority on system safety. You set the safety philosophy, risk acceptance posture, and analytical standards that apply across every division, and you are the person leadership turns to when a safety question is consequential, contested, or without precedent.
  • This role exists to make sure Anduril does not build systems it cannot certify, field, or defend. You will provide independent safety assessments of programs at any point in their lifecycle, carrying the same rigor a government weapon system safety review board would apply. You will engage programs early, before architecture is locked, so design decisions that are difficult to undo are caught while they are still cheap to change. And you will serve as a senior resource the company can deploy wherever deep system safety judgment is needed most.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Serve as a company-wide System Safety technical authority across all Anduril divisions, setting direction that spans Air Dominance & Strike, Maritime, Ground Systems, Space, Counter-UAS, and Autonomy/Lattice rather than a single program or product line
  • Conduct independent, end-to-end safety assessments of any program at any lifecycle phase
  • Deploy as a senior technical resource to programs across the portfolio, standing up a credible System Safety approach quickly and leaving behind a baseline the program team can sustain
  • Prepare programs and their engineering teams for formal government safety certification
  • Shape Anduril's enterprise technical risk posture by introducing the analytical models, hazard framing, and risk acceptance philosophy that leadership uses to make fielding, test, and investment decisions
  • Pioneer analysis and verification approaches for emerging technology, including autonomous and AI/ML-enabled systems, where MIL-STD-882E and existing frameworks do not provide sufficient coverage
  • Negotiate safety acceptance criteria, alternate means of compliance, and tailored standards with customers, service safety centers, and regulatory authorities on behalf of the company
  • Drive System Safety philosophy, planning standards, and requirements practice across the enterprise, and influence customer and regulatory requirements for novel systems
  • Grow Senior and Staff System Safety engineers into recognized experts and create the frameworks, mental models, and training for engineers across the company
  • Represent Anduril externally as a thought leader in industry working groups, standards bodies, and customer safety forums

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Minimum of 15 years of industry experience as a System Safety Engineer or equivalent engineering background
  • B.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or equivalent technical discipline
  • Direct experience with government safety review boards such as the Weapon System Explosives Safety Review Board (WSESRB), Nonnuclear Munitions Safety Board (NNMSB), and Software System Safety Technical Review Panel (SSSTRP) including building the safety case, presenting it, and achieving board approval
  • Deep experience with safety-critical hardware and software systems in the defense or aerospace industry, with a preference for Weapon Systems, Aircraft, UAS, Maritime, Space, Munitions and Energetics, or Rotorcraft
  • Expert-level knowledge of MIL-STD-882E, including the judgment to tailor it credibly, and working familiarity with service-level system safety policy and the Joint Software Systems Safety Engineering Handbook (JSSSEH)
  • Expert background in safety analysis techniques including FTA, FHA, SCFTA, and FMECA, with the judgment to know when each technique is the wrong tool for the problem
  • Failure investigation and analysis experience with a proven track record of solving problems and preventing reoccurrence
  • Extensive Design Review experience (PDR, CDR, MRR) and confident presentation skills across all levels of leadership, including executives, customers, and external safety authorities
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills and excellent communication skills, with the ability to build influence across organizations where you have no formal authority
  • Willingness to travel between Anduril sites, customer locations, and test ranges to support programs across the portfolio
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • M.S. or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or equivalent technical discipline
  • AI/ML and autonomy safety experience, including run-time assurance and the safety implications of DoD autonomous weapon system policy (strongly preferred)
  • Experience with Relyence, Teamcenter, JIRA, JAMA, Cameo, and/or Ansys

ABOUT THE TEAM

Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build and deploy the full technology stack that powers Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, the manufacturing execution system (ArsenalOS) that workers and planners use every shift, the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that eliminate manual toil from both the shop floor and business operations.

MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology. Our systems live where factory-floor machines, edge compute, and OT networks meet enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure. We incubate solutions close to the production line, validate them with real operators building real hardware, harden them for reliability and security, and then scale them across multiple sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship.

This is not a support function. It is a strategic investment by Anduril in the premise that digitizing the manufacturing lifecycle end-to-end, from engineering definition through scheduling through execution through field feedback, is how Heavy Metal will out-build, out-adapt, and out-scale the traditional defense industrial base. MDP is scaling from a founding team to 70+ engineers across multiple U.S. sites. You will be joining early, working on hard problems with real operational stakes, and shaping how manufacturing software is built at Anduril from the ground up.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Machine Learning Engineer on the Applied Intelligence initiative, you will be the critical bridge between ML research and production operations. You will own the infrastructure that brings ML prototypes from concept to reliable, production-grade systems running on factory floors and serving manufacturing teams. Working at the intersection of data engineering, MLOps, and production operations, you'll execute the vision of ML engineers by building robust datasets, training infrastructure, and inference systems that operate reliably in both cloud and on-premises OT environments.
This role requires someone who can translate ML requirements into production infrastructure, coordinate across teams (data engineering, Big Anduril, manufacturing operations), and serve as the on-call owner for deployed ML systems. You'll be responsible for ensuring that AI applications don't just work in demos—they work 24/7 in real manufacturing environments where downtime has real consequences.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Infrastructure Ownership & Production Operations

  • Own production hardening and deployment of ML prototype applications, transforming research concepts into reliable, maintainable production systems
  • Take part in on-call rotations for deployed ML products running on factory floors and serving Mantech, ensuring high availability and rapid incident response
  • Build and maintain inference infrastructure across cloud environments and on-premises OT hardware deployed on the factory floor
  • Deploy and operate ML systems in factory environments, including edge compute clusters and OT networks, with a focus on reliability and observability
  • Implement comprehensive monitoring, alerting, and drift detection systems to maintain operational SLOs for production ML applications
  • Define and execute rollback procedures, validation gates, and safety reviews for AI systems in production

Cross-Functional Coordination & Requirements Translation

  • Interface directly with the data engineering team to define and deliver ML-specific data infrastructure needs for Applied Intelligence
  • Coordinate with Anduril enterprise teams to secure compute resources, labeling infrastructure, data access, and modeling capabilities needed for ML initiatives
  • Execute the technical vision of ML engineers by translating their requirements into concrete infrastructure for datasets, training pipelines, and inference systems
  • Partner with manufacturing engineers and factory operators to understand production workflows and translate them into MLOps requirements
  • Drive make/buy decisions by evaluating internal and vendor capabilities against Applied Intelligence needs

Platform & Infrastructure Development

  • Architect and own the end-to-end ML platform stack—from data ingestion and labeling through training orchestration to model serving and lifecycle management
  • Build model-serving and inference frameworks optimized for production environments, supporting real-time and batch execution across cloud, edge, and shop-floor systems
  • Implement event-driven data pipelines and telemetry systems that feed models with contextualized, real-time signals from factory sensors and production systems
  • Select, prioritize, and standardize MLOps components including feature stores, vector databases, model registries, orchestration layers, and observability systems
  • Design training infrastructure that enables ML engineers to iterate quickly while maintaining reproducibility and governance

Data & Model Lifecycle Management

  • Own dataset creation, curation, versioning, and management processes that enable high-quality model development
  • Implement model governance processes for validation, traceability, retraining triggers, and version control
  • Build systems for data labeling workflows, quality assurance, and continuous data pipeline monitoring
  • Manage model versioning, experiment tracking, and artifact management across development and production environments

Code Quality & Team Practices

  • Write production-quality code with comprehensive tests, participating in code review and architectural discussions
  • Establish best practices for MLOps, observability, data management, and secure handling of sensitive production data
  • Leverage AI tooling (coding assistants, automation) in your development workflow and contribute to team engineering practices
  • Mentor junior engineers and data scientists on production ML best practices

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 6+ years of experience in software engineering or ML engineering roles building production systems, ideally in fast-paced environments
  • Strong production MLOps experience: data pipeline management, model versioning, deployment automation, and production monitoring
  • Proven track record of taking ML models from prototype to production and maintaining them long-term
  • Experience with on-call rotations and production incident management for data or ML systems
  • Strong proficiency in Python and experience with deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow)
  • Experience building and deploying containerized ML services using Docker and Kubernetes
  • Solid data engineering skills including pipeline orchestration, data quality management, and working with time-series or event-driven data

Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. Maritime Digital Production is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build and deploy the technology stack that powers Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, the manufacturing execution system that workers and planners use every shift, the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that remove manual toil from the shop floor and business operations. That includes Serapis, our program building components for the Virginia-class submarine.

We operate at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology, incubating solutions close to the production line, validating them with real operators, hardening them for reliability and security, and scaling them across sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship.

We are scaling from a founding team to more than 70 engineers across multiple U.S. sites. As an intern you join early, on a problem that matters to production, with a defined project and a named engineer you work with every day.

We have built a computational geometry engine that takes a 3D CAD assembly and works out the orders in which it can physically come apart, and therefore the orders in which it can be built. It finds where parts touch, builds directional blocking graphs from that contact geometry, searches for collision-free removal directions, and produces the precedence constraints our production scheduling system plans against.

It works on small and mid-sized assemblies. It needs to work on the assemblies we actually build, which have hundreds to thousands of parts. Your job is to close that gap.

This is algorithms engineering with a research flavor. You will profile the engine on real assemblies, find where the time and memory go, and attack it: search ordering, pruning, memorization, incremental updates, subassembly decomposition, and parallelism. The goal is a measurably faster engine rather than a paper, and every result is held to one rule: a faster answer that is a different answer is a bug.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Profiling a C++ computational geometry pipeline on real assemblies and reporting where time and memory go
  • Designing and implementing algorithmic improvements to a disassembly sequence search: candidate ordering, pruning, memoization, and incremental graph updates
  • Decomposing large assemblies into subassemblies that can be solved independently
  • Parallelizing expensive geometric tests across cores without losing determinism
  • Building a benchmark corpus and harness that run in continuous integration and catch regressions
  • Gating every optimization on output equivalence against a reference set
  • Writing up results and presenting them to the engineering team

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Must be pursuing master’s degree or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related field.
  • Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program.
  • Ability to complete an in-person co-op in Santa Ana, CA, in winter 2027.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Strong modern C++, C++17 or later. You have written and debugged performance-sensitive C++ in a codebase you did not write yourself, not only coursework.
  • Solid algorithms and data structures, including graph algorithms such as strongly connected components and topological ordering, combinatorial search and pruning, and complexity analysis.
  • Computational geometry fundamentals: triangle meshes, bounding volume hierarchies and other spatial indexes, intersection and collision tests, and reasoning about directions on the sphere.
  • Experience profiling and optimizing code. You have used a profiler and made something measurably faster.
  • Research or coursework in assembly sequence planning, disassembly planning, or motion planning. If you know what a non-directional blocking graph is, or have read Wilson and Latombe or the STAAT work by Romney and colleagues, we want to talk to you.
  • Publications at ICRA, IROS, RSS, SoCG, or Solid and Physical Modeling, or in the Computer-Aided Design journal.
  • Experience with Eigen, OpenCASCADE, OpenVDB, CGAL, or a collision or bounding volume hierarchy library.
  • Parallel programming in C++ with Intel TBB, OpenMP, or standard threads, with attention to determinism.
  • Familiarity with CAD data: boundary representations versus tessellated meshes, and formats such as STEP and JT.
  • Experience with CMake, GoogleTest, and reproducible builds. Nix is a plus.
  • Python for tooling and analysis, e.g. NumPy and trimesh.
  • Familiarity with infinitesimal motion analysis or rotational motions in assembly planning.

ABOUT THE ROLE:
As a Site Reliability Engineer focused on campus reliability, you will design what the campus watches and trusts, technically command cross-discipline SEVs, and build the guardrails that make the next incident smaller. You are the connective tissue across compute, network, storage, power, and cooling on one of the largest AI training campuses in the world. This role demands calm incident leadership, fleet-scale observability judgment, and the ability to drive reliability work across software and facility boundaries. We are looking for candidates from power plants, nuclear power plants, data centers, or people who currently work or have worked in facilities like SpaceXSI with power, compute, cooling, and related plant systems.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own monitoring architecture and signal quality across GPU and host telemetry (DCGM, Prometheus/Grafana) and facility telemetry (BMS, EPMS, DCIM, SCADA, CDU / direct liquid cooling): what we alert on, suppress, and trust. Consume NOC noise-disposition feedback to drive suppression and redesign. Treat alert noise as a design failure, not an operator failure.
  • Provide SEV command support: technical incident leadership, bridge coordination with the NOC, paging and escalation (e.g., PagerDuty), and timeline and severity hygiene.
  • Run blameless postmortems and drive corrective actions to closed, not filed.
  • Gate high-risk change: fleet-scale firmware/BIOS/BMC rollouts (Redfish, canaries, rollback) and SOP/MOP/EOP-governed work on power and cooling systems through a disciplined change management process.
  • Lead cross-functional reliability projects spanning compute, network (InfiniBand/RoCE), storage, and facility signal boundaries, including grey failures that cross those boundaries (e.g., NVLink flapping, thermal throttling, power sequencing).
  • Partner with Hardware Failure Analysis on systemic failure classes: turn fleet data (MTBF/AFR, repeat-RMA trends) into monitoring, stop-rules, and vendor RCA inputs.
  • Build and maintain playbooks, run game days, and keep cross-discipline dependency maps current. Own runbook quality jointly with the NOC (SRE designs; NOC operates and corrects).
  • Define error budgets and availability objectives at campus and service boundaries as adopted by the business.
  • Participate in on-call rotations and incident response for SEV-class events in the Memphis / Southaven data center campus.

PROFILE SIGNALS:

  • Experience in power plants, nuclear power plants, data centers, or facilities like SpaceXSI — current or prior — spanning power, compute, cooling, or related plant systems.
  • Proven large-scale incident command experience and calm technical leadership on a bridge. Nuclear control-room, shift supervisor / Senior Reactor Operator (SRO), Shift Technical Advisor, or Navy nuclear experience counts as incident command.
  • Demonstrated monitoring and observability design at fleet or campus scale, including alert hygiene, suppression, and signal quality. Treats alert noise as a design failure, not an operator failure.
  • Cross-team facilitation and systems engineering depth across software and facility boundaries.

SUCCESS MEASURED BY:

  • MTTD / MTTR trend for SEV-class events
  • % of SEVs with a blameless postmortem and closed action items
  • Alert actionable ratio
  • Recurrence rate of incident classes
  • Monitoring coverage of critical dependencies across compute, network, storage, power, and cooling
  • GPU fleet availability lost to infrastructure events

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 5+ years of experience in site reliability, systems engineering, plant operations, or large-scale production operations, preferably in power plants, nuclear power plants, high-performance computing, or data center environments.
  • Proven large-scale incident command experience and calm technical leadership on a bridge, whether from an SRE/NOC bridge or a plant control room.
  • Demonstrated monitoring and observability design at fleet or campus scale, including alert hygiene, suppression, and signal quality.
  • Hands-on experience with at least one of: Prometheus/Grafana, NVIDIA DCGM, or industrial telemetry and controls (SCADA, BMS/BAS, EPMS, DCIM, PLCs, Modbus/BACnet).
  • Experience working across at least two of: compute, network, storage, power, and cooling / facilities telemetry.
  • Experience writing and operating playbooks, runbooks, or SOP/MOP/EOPs with a 24/7 operations, control room, or NOC partner.
  • Proficiency in scripting (Python, Bash) for automation and analysis, plus general experience in at least one systems language (C, C++, Java, Go, Rust, or similar). Not required to be expert in all of them.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills with a data-driven approach to reliability engineering.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams, including NOC, data center operations, hardware failure analysis, and infrastructure engineering.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Experience in power plants, nuclear power plants, or other high-consequence industrial control environments (ICS/OT).
  • Current or prior work in data centers or facilities like SpaceXSI spanning power, compute, cooling, and related plant systems, including CDU / direct liquid cooling.
  • Experience in AI/ML infrastructure or supercomputing environments: GB200/NVL72 or H100/H200-class GPU fleets, NCCL, InfiniBand/RoCE, Slurm or Kubernetes.
  • Fleet firmware and BMC management (Redfish, IPMI), including firmware release validation and staged rollouts.
  • Reliability engineering methods: MTBF/AFR analysis, reliability-centered maintenance, grey-failure diagnosis, and vendor RCA/RMA partnership.
  • Experience with CMMS (e.g., Maximo) and commissioning / integrated systems testing (IST) and operational turnover.
  • Hands-on definition and use of SLOs, SLIs, and error budgets at service or campus boundaries.
  • Experience running game days, dependency mapping, and closed-loop corrective action programs.
  • Familiarity with data center hardware and plant signals (servers, GPUs, networking, power, cooling) in addition to software telemetry.
  • Prior work in a fast-paced startup or tech company like SpaceXSI.

Role Overview:

At Cohere, we believe in the power of multimodal AI to revolutionise the way we interact with technology. Our engineering teams push the boundaries of what's possible, and we're looking for talented individuals to join us on this exciting journey. With an exceptional ratio of compute resources to engineers, we provide an ideal environment for you to explore, innovate and shape the future of AI.

On July 31st 2025, Cohere's Multimodal team Introduced Command A Vision: Multimodal AI Built for Business. At release our new flagship vision-language model:
● Consistently outperforms major models like Llama 4 Maverick, Mistral Medium/Pixtral Large, and GPT4.1

● Built for the real world - 112B parameters running on just 2 GPUs

With a focused team, breakthrough performance doesn't require breakthrough compute. Focus on the things that matter, and join the team. This role is perfect for you if you:

  • Have a deep passion for machine learning and its potential to impact various industries through multimodal applications.

  • Are comfortable diving into complex ML codebases to identify and resolve issues, ensuring the smooth operation of our systems.

  • Thrive in a fast-paced, technically challenging environment, where you can contribute your innovative ideas and solutions.

  • Have a history of delivering creative, practical solutions to real-world problems, demonstrating your ability to think outside the box.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design and develop cutting-edge multimodal AI systems, integrating various modalities such as text, speech, and vision.

  • Conduct research and experiments on our advanced compute infrastructure, exploring novel ideas in multimodal representation learning, transfer learning, and more.

  • Collaborate closely with our world-class teams, learning from and contributing to their expertise in the field.

  • Possess exceptional software engineering skills, with a proven track record of building robust and scalable systems.

  • Have a strong command of Python and are well-versed in popular deep learning frameworks like JAX, PyTorch, and TensorFlow, with an understanding of their multimodal capabilities.

  • Knowledge of distributed training strategies, especially for large-scale multimodal models.

If you're excited about the potential of multimodal AI and want to be at the forefront of this rapidly evolving field, we want to hear from you! Join us at Cohere and be a part of a diverse, remote-friendly team that's changing the world of AI.

Cohere is a fast-growing company in the extremely dynamic artificial intelligence space. We are building a Government Affairs and Public Policy (GAPP) team that has the drive and experience to engage in and shape a nascent and unique policy environment for enterprise AI.

We seek a Government Affairs professional to lead our US government affairs strategy, with the flexibility to help shape our policy footprint across key emerging markets in the Americas as our commercial presence grows. Candidates will have a proven track record, are analytical, collaborative, driven, and possess a passion for digging deep into the new and evolving public policy debate at the intersection of enterprise technology and artificial intelligence.

There is no better time to join us in building this function as we shape the future of AI in the United States and across the region.

In this role you will:

  • Lead US Advocacy: Partner closely with Cohere’s senior leadership, legal, public policy, and responsible AI teams to develop, coordinate, and implement a government affairs strategy across both US federal and state levels. For the right leader, there is opportunity to expand this advocacy to support our strategic growth across Latin America.

You will proactively report on trends and work with cross-functional teams to craft thoughtful responses to governmental initiatives, regulatory issues, and legislative drafts that impact Cohere’s business.

  • Deep AI Policy Expertise: Exceptional ability to dig deep on artificial intelligence policy, its applications, and its risks, with a proven track record of shaping relevant tech policies and regulations.

The team combines expertise in software engineering, machine learning, and low-level kernel design and development to design robust systems and enhance model performance. You will work on identifying and removing performance bottlenecks, develop cutting-edge training and profiling tools to help Cohere's mission of providing efficient and reliable language understanding and generation capabilities and drive innovation in the field of natural language processing.

  • Research, implement, and experiment with ideas on our supercompute and data infrastructure.

About Cohere and North

Cohere is revolutionizing enterprise AI with North, an agentic AI platform designed to securely deploy AI agents and automations within organizations' infrastructure. North empowers employees to streamline workflows, automate repetitive tasks, and unlock actionable insights while ensuring data privacy and compliance. North combines cutting-edge generative and search models with customizable integrations to drive productivity and innovation at scale.

Role Overview

We are seeking an Agent Harness Product Manager to own the execution layer that makes North agents reliable, capable, and production-ready. This is a role that sits at the intersection of three domains:

Agent Loop and Execution.

Own the core agent runtime: tool orchestration, parallel execution, sub-agent delegation, sandbox code execution, and failure recovery. You will define how North agents plan and act across long, multi-step workflows and ensure the execution environment is robust enough for the most demanding enterprise tasks. You are expected to engage at the implementation level, contributing to architecture decisions alongside engineering rather than simply handing off requirements.

Context Engineering.

Own how our Agents manage the context window as a deliberately controlled resource. This includes progressive disclosure of tools and skills, context compaction and summarization, offloading of large payloads to a persistent filesystem, and the instrumentation that keeps agents oriented across extended trajectories.

Model-Scaffolding Co-evolution.

Own the feedback loop between North's harness and the Modeling Team. This PM is the connective tissue that makes that possible: ensuring harness design decisions are validated by Modeling before they are built, that evals are the shared bridge between both teams, and that as the harness evolves the model evolves with it.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own the roadmap for North's agent harness, including the agent loop, context engineering layer, tool orchestration, sandbox execution, and sub-agent delegation

  • Serve as the primary interface between North engineering and Cohere's Modeling team, ensuring new harness capabilities are validated before being built and that neither team paints itself into a corner

  • Own North's agentic evaluation framework, ensuring evals are compatible with both the North harness and Modeling's training infrastructure, and that they serve as a reliable bridge between product and research

  • Engage enterprise customers to surface real-world agentic failures and translate findings into concrete product and model requirements

  • Partner with the agentic expert modeling team to define goals that maximize the impact of our models and prioritize model capabilities and evals most critical for delivering on those goals. Establish a clear roadmap for our agentic modeling capabilities.

  • Stay current with the open-source and commercial agent ecosystem and drive adoption decisions that keep North's architecture aligned with emerging standards.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of product management experience as a research PM, in agentic AI systems,, or applied ML products

  • Deep understanding of agentic harnesses, including the latest paid and open source offerings.

  • Deep understanding of modern LLM agent architectures, including multi-agent systems, tool-augmented reasoning, memory and retrieval, programmatic orchestration, RAG, and long-horizon execution

  • Strong grasp of agentic evaluation design, including how to measure task completion, failure recovery, and long-horizon reliability, and how to diagnose model vs. scaffolding gaps

  • Technically deep enough to contribute to architecture decisions at the implementation level: comfortable reviewing and shaping design docs, reasoning about async execution patterns, sandboxed environments, filesystem design, and the tradeoffs that come with building harness capabilities into a production platform

  • Ability to flex between ML research conversations and engineering architecture discussions with equal fluency

  • Track record of shipping platform-layer products with demonstrated impact on reliability, performance, or capability.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Direct experience in developing and shipping leading agentic harnesses.

  • An active practitioner of agent frameworks who regularly builds with and follows the latest developments in open-source harnesses, coding agents, and orchestration tools in both professional and personal work

  • Hands-on experience with enterprise agentic deployments: multi-tenant orchestration, tool permissioning, audit trails, and compliance requirements

  • Prior work at the intersection of research and product, translating nascent model capabilities into shipped product features

  • Background working within or closely alongside an ML research or post-training team.

Why this role?

The Data Infrastructure team at Cohere is responsible for the storage and data movement layer underlying every model training run. We're building the unified storage layer that feeds our training workloads. It needs to serve petabytes of training data and model checkpoints fast enough to keep thousands of GPUs busy across several training clusters. In this role, you’d have an opportunity to build this system from the ground up. You’d be a key contributor, working on a problem few teams have had to solve at this scale.

In this role, you will:

  • Design, build, and operate the distributed storage system that feeds model training and evaluation.

  • Run this system multiple on Kubernetes clusters at petabyte scale.

  • Work with researchers and training-infra teams on how jobs actually read and write data, and turn that into throughput, latency, and durability requirements

  • Work through the networking, I/O, and consistency problems of moving large datasets and checkpoints across regions and backends, with GPU idle time and time-to-insight as the measures of success

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • Strong storage fundamentals, including replication, consistency, caching, and data lifecycle management.

  • Strong coding ability. We work in Python and Go; experience in either is enough, but you should be willing to pick up the other

  • Experience running stateful systems on Kubernetes, including Persistent Volumes, CSI drivers, and StatefulSets.

  • Hands-on experience with cloud object storage such as S3 as well as POSIX-style filesystems.

It’s a bonus if you have:

  • Experience with parallel or HPC filesystems such as Weka, VAST, or Lustre.

  • Familiarity with the data-loading and checkpointing patterns used in large-scale model training.

  • An interest in how large models are trained and evaluated, including the trajectory and eval data those runs generate, and a desire to understand the workloads the platform is serving.

As a Manager of Security Engineering, your key responsibilities include:

  • Serve as trusted advisor to team’s leadership and partner teams by clearly articulating business risks associated with security issues

  • Execute the long-term vision for the Security team in alignment with Cohere’s product and business goals.

  • Collaborate closely with leadership to prioritize high-impact initiatives and strategic customer engagements.

  • Vulnerability Management: Develop and implement enterprise-wide vulnerability management processes and tooling, including identification, prioritization, remediation tracking, and reporting, including customer artifacts

  • Static Application Security Testing (SAST): Establish SAST programs, integrate tools into CI/CD pipelines, and analyze results to identify and remediate security flaws in source code

  • Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST): Implement DAST methodologies, configure scanning tools, and conduct regular assessments of running applications

  • Penetration Testing: Lead and oversee internal and external penetration testing engagements, including web application, API, network and agentic AI platform including managing our bug bounty program

  • Security Architecture Review: Collaborate with development teams to review and validate security architecture and design patterns

  • Secure SDLC Integration: Embed security practices throughout the software development lifecycle, working closely with engineering and product teams

  • Team Leadership: Lead and grow a high-performing team of Security engineers through hiring, coaching, and mentorship

  • Metrics and Reporting: Establish key security metrics, generate regular reports for leadership, and communicate security posture to stakeholders

  • Compliance and Standards: Ensure application security practices align with industry standards (OWASP Top10 for LLMs, ISO 27001) and regulatory requirements

You may be a good fit if:

  • You have 8+ years of previous experience in Application Security / Security Engineering with a strong focus on vulnerability management, SDLC and bug bounty programs.

  • Proven experience with SAST, DAST, and penetration testing methodologies and tools

  • Proficiency with programming languages (Python, GoLang, etc.) and web technologies

  • Experience with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure) and container security

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with ability to influence technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • Experience building and managing high-performing security teams

  • You are comfortable with ambiguity and are able to make informed decisions with little data.

  • You employ a flexible and constructive approach when solving problems.

  • You are able to make trade-offs between build vs. buy decisions—help build solutions and be able to review what tools are available.

  • You understand secure engineering best practices, can articulate problem statements, and propose solutions to both technically savvy and non-technical audiences.

  • You have a deep technical understanding of common security vulnerabilities and risks, as well as countermeasures and compensating controls.
